import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
items = {
    "Alpha": 55,
    "Beta": 66,
    "Gamma": 56,
    "Delta": 65,
    "Epsilon": 35,
    "Zeta": 46,
    "Eta": 60,
    "Theta": 44,
    "Iota": 37,
    "Kappa": 48,
    "Lambda": 39,
    "Mu": 53,
    "Nu": 36,
    "Xi": 38,
    "Omicron": 33,
    "Pi": 38,
    "Rho": 67,
    "Sigma": 65,
    "Tau": 42,
    "Upsilon": 30,
    "Phi": 32,
    "Chi": 55,
}

# Number of possible crates (upper bound = number of items)
n_items = len(items)
item_names = list(items.keys())
mass = [items[name] for name in item_names]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("crate_allocation", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Binary variable y_k = 1 if crate k is used
y = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("y", range(n_items), cat="Binary")

# Binary variable x_i_k = 1 if item i is placed in crate k
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("x", (range(n_items), range(n_items)), cat="Binary")

# Objective: minimise number of used crates
model += pulp.lpSum(y[k] for k in range(n_items))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Every item must be assigned to exactly one crate
for i in range(n_items):
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[i][k] for k in range(n_items)) == 1

# 2) Capacity of each crate (100) cannot be exceeded
for k in range(n_items):
    model += pulp.lpSum(mass[i] * x[i][k] for i in range(n_items)) <= 100 * y[k]

# 3) Linking: an item can be placed in a crate only if that crate is used
for i in range(n_items):
    for k in range(n_items):
        model += x[i][k] <= y[k]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
used_crates = [k for k in range(n_items) if pulp.value(y[k]) > 0.5]
print(f"Minimum number of crates required: {len(used_crates)}\n")

for k in used_crates:
    assigned_items = [item_names[i] for i in range(n_items) if pulp.value(x[i][k]) > 0.5]
    total_mass = sum(items[name] for name in assigned_items)
    print(f"Crate {k+1}:")
    print(f"  Items ({len(assigned_items)}): {', '.join(assigned_items)}")
    print(f"  Total mass: {total_mass}\n")

# Bin‑packing model for allocating research equipment components to transport crates
# Author: generated by ChatGPT
# Solver: HiGHS (via PuLP)

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
items = {
    "Alpha":   55,
    "Beta":    66,
    "Gamma":   56,
    "Delta":   65,
    "Epsilon": 35,
    "Zeta":    46,
    "Eta":     60,
    "Theta":   44,
    "Iota":    37,
    "Kappa":   48,
    "Lambda":  39,
    "Mu":      53,
    "Nu":      36,
    "Xi":      38,
    "Omicron": 33,
    "Pi":      38,
    "Rho":     67,
    "Sigma":   65,
    "Tau":     42,
    "Upsilon": 30,
    "Phi":     32,
    "Chi":     55,
}

capacity = 100                     # maximum mass per crate
n_items = len(items)               # 22
max_bins = n_items                 # a trivial upper bound (one item per bin)

item_names = list(items.keys())
item_weights = [items[name] for name in item_names]
item_idx = range(n_items)
bin_idx   = range(max_bins)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("MinCrates", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Binary variable y_k : 1 if crate k is used
y = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("crate_used", bin_idx, lowBound=0, upBound=1, cat=pulp.LpBinary)

# Binary variable x_i_k : 1 if item i is placed in crate k
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "assign",
    ((i, k) for i in item_idx for k in bin_idx),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# Objective: minimise number of used crates
model += pulp.lpSum(y[k] for k in bin_idx), "TotalCrates"

# Constraint 1: every item assigned to exactly one crate
for i in item_idx:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, k)] for k in bin_idx) == 1, f"AssignItem_{i}"

# Constraint 2: capacity of each crate
for k in bin_idx:
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(item_weights[i] * x[(i, k)] for i in item_idx)
        <= capacity * y[k]
    ), f"Capacity_{k}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Solver status: {status}")

if status == "Optimal":
    used_bins = [k for k in bin_idx if pulp.value(y[k]) > 0.5]
    print(f"Minimum number of crates required: {len(used_bins)}\n")

    # Build a readable allocation
    allocation = {k: [] for k in used_bins}
    for i in item_idx:
        for k in used_bins:
            if pulp.value(x[(i, k)]) > 0.5:
                allocation[k].append(item_names[i])
                break

    for k in used_bins:
        items_in_bin = allocation[k]
        total_mass = sum(items[name] for name in items_in_bin)
        print(f"Crate {k+1}:")
        for name in items_in_bin:
            print(f"  - {name} (mass {items[name]})")
        print(f"  Total mass = {total_mass}\n")
else:
    print("No optimal solution found.")

max_bins = num_items               # upper bound: one item per crate

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# Decision variables

x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    ((i, k) for i in range(num_items) for k in range(max_bins)),
    cat="Binary"
)

# y[k] = 1 if crate k is used, else 0
y = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "y",
    (k for k in range(max_bins)),
    cat="Binary"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

    "Upsilon": 30,
    "Phi":     32,
    "Chi":     55,
}
capacity = 100                     # maximum load per crate
n_items = len(items)
max_bins = n_items                 # worst‑case upper bound (one item per crate)

# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("equipment_crate_allocation", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Binary decision variables:
#   x[(i,k)] = 1 if item i is placed in crate k
#   y[k]     = 1 if crate k is used
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    ((i, k) for i in items for k in range(max_bins)),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)
y = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "y",
    (k for k in range(max_bins)),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# Objective: minimise the number of crates used
model += pulp.lpSum(y[k] for k in range(max_bins)), "Minimize_number_of_crates"

# Constraint 1: each item must be assigned to exactly one crate
for i in items:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, k)] for k in range(max_bins)) == 1, f"Assign_{i}_once"

# Constraint 2: crate capacity (only active if the crate is used)
for k in range(max_bins):
    model += pulp.lpSum(items[i] * x[(i, k)] for i in items) <= capacity * y[k], f"Capacity_bin_{k}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

packages = {
    "Alpha":   68,

    "Epsilon": 48,

    "Eta":     68,

    "Iota":    60,
    "Kappa":   54,
    "Lambda":  68,
    "Mu":      67,
    "Nu":      44,
    "Xi":      31,
}

capacity = 100                     # truck capacity (kg)
n_packages = len(packages)
max_trucks = n_packages            # worst‑case upper bound (one package per truck)

pkg_names = list(packages.keys())
weights   = [packages[p] for p in pkg_names]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Min_Trucks", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
# y[k] = 1 if truck k is used
y = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("TruckUsed", range(max_trucks), lowBound=0, upBound=1, cat=pulp.LpBinary)

# x[i,k] = 1 if package i is placed on truck k
x = {}
for i in range(n_packages):
    for k in range(max_trucks):
        var_name = f"Assign_{pkg_names[i]}_toTruck_{k}"
        x[(i, k)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, lowBound=0, upBound=1, cat=pulp.LpBinary)

# Objective: minimise the number of trucks used
model += pulp.lpSum(y[k] for k in range(max_trucks)), "Total_Trucks_Used"

for i in range(n_packages):
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, k)] for k in range(max_trucks)) == 1, f"OneTruck_{pkg_names[i]}"

# 2) Weight on each truck cannot exceed its capacity; if the truck is not used, weight must be 0
for k in range(max_trucks):
    model += pulp.lpSum(weights[i] * x[(i, k)] for i in range(n_packages)) <= capacity * y[k], f"CapTruck_{k}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

        total_w = sum(packages[p] for p in assigned)

    69, 40, 55, 31, 34, 41, 54
]

# Model data
N = len(names)                 # number of shipments = 31
K = N                          # upper bound on aircraft needed (one per shipment)
capacity = 100                 # payload limit per aircraft (tonnes)

# --------------------------------------------------
# Build the model
import pulp

model = pulp.LpProblem("Aircraft_Bin_Packing", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
# x[i,k] = 1 if shipment i is placed on aircraft k
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    ((i, k) for i in range(N) for k in range(K)),
    lowBound=0, upBound=1, cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# y[k] = 1 if aircraft k is used
y = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "y",
    (k for k in range(K)),
    lowBound=0, upBound=1, cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# Objective: minimise the number of aircraft used
model += pulp.lpSum(y[k] for k in range(K))

# --------------------------------------------------
# Constraints

# 1) Every shipment must be assigned to exactly one aircraft
for i in range(N):
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, k)] for k in range(K)) == 1

# 2) Aircraft capacity must not be exceeded
for k in range(K):
    model += pulp.lpSum(masses[i] * x[(i, k)] for i in range(N)) <= capacity * y[k]

# 3) Linking: a shipment can only be placed on a used aircraft
for i in range(N):
    for k in range(K):
        model += x[(i, k)] <= y[k]

# 4) Symmetry breaking – force used aircraft to occupy the lowest indices
for k in range(K - 1):
    model += y[k] >= y[k + 1]

# --------------------------------------------------
# Solve with HiGHS (time limit 120 s, no solver messages)
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

    for k in range(K):

    for i in range(N):
        for k in range(K):

                assignments[k].append(names[i])
                break

    # Print each aircraft's load

        load = sum(masses[names.index(s)] for s in assignments[k])
        print(f"Aircraft {k + 1} (load = {load} t): {', '.join(assignments[k])}")

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Bin‑packing model for loading 36 packages (given volumes) into identical trucks
with capacity 100 cu‑ft.  The model minimizes the number of trucks used.
Implemented with PuLP and the HiGHS MILP solver.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
volumes = [
    44, 43, 34, 57, 52, 64, 34, 40, 41, 70,
    69, 44, 65, 35, 48, 62, 54, 33, 70, 52,
    43, 59, 67, 66, 42, 59, 62, 36, 58, 42,
    52, 68, 50, 51, 68, 69
]                         # index 0 … 35 corresponds to Package 1 … 36
n_packages = len(volumes)
truck_capacity = 100

# Upper bound on the number of trucks needed: one per package (worst case)
max_trucks = n_packages

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Truck_Loading_Minimize_Trucks", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
# x[i][k] = 1 if package i is placed in truck k
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    ((i, k) for i in range(n_packages) for k in range(max_trucks)),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# y[k] = 1 if truck k is used
y = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "y",
    (k for k in range(max_trucks)),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimize total number of trucks used
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += pulp.lpSum(y[k] for k in range(max_trucks)), "Minimize_trucks"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Each package must be assigned to exactly one truck
for i in range(n_packages):
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(x[i, k] for k in range(max_trucks)) == 1,
        f"AssignPackage_{i+1}",
    )

# 2) The total volume in a truck cannot exceed its capacity;
#    if a truck is not used (y[k]=0) the RHS becomes 0, forcing x[i,k]=0
for k in range(max_trucks):
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(volumes[i] * x[i, k] for i in range(n_packages))
        <= truck_capacity * y[k],
        f"CapacityTruck_{k+1}",
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output results
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Solver status: {status}")

if status == "Optimal":
    # Determine which trucks are actually used
    used_trucks = [k for k in range(max_trucks) if pulp.value(y[k]) > 0.5]
    print(f"Minimum number of trucks required: {len(used_trucks)}\n")

    # Build a readable assignment list
    assignments = {k: [] for k in used_trucks}
    for i in range(n_packages):
        for k in used_trucks:
            if pulp.value(x[i, k]) > 0.5:
                assignments[k].append(i + 1)   # package numbers are 1‑based
                break

    # Print the load of each used truck
    for k in used_trucks:
        pkgs = assignments[k]
        total_vol = sum(volumes[p - 1] for p in pkgs)
        print(f"Truck {k+1} (used): Packages {pkgs}, Total volume = {total_vol} cu‑ft")
else:
    print("No optimal solution found.")

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Bin‑packing model for allocating shipments to identical pallets (capacity 100 kg)
and minimizing the number of pallets used.

Each shipment must be placed on exactly one pallet and the total weight on a
pallet cannot exceed 100 kg.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# List of shipments (name, mass in kg)
shipments = [
    ("Alpha",   48),
    ("Beta",    56),
    ("Gamma",   58),
    ("Delta",   62),
    ("Epsilon", 48),
    ("Zeta",    34),
    ("Eta",     32),
    ("Theta",   35),
    ("Iota",    52),
    ("Kappa",   54),
    ("Lambda",  56),
    ("Mu",      54),
    ("Nu",      70),
    ("Xi",      44),
    ("Omicron", 48),
    ("Pi",      61),
    ("Rho",     55),
    ("Sigma",   65),
    ("Tau",     30),
    ("Upsilon", 70),
    ("Phi",     57),
    ("Chi",     70),
    ("Psi",     48),
    ("Omega",   61),
    ("Aa",      39),
    ("Bb",      55),
    ("Cc",      57),
    ("Dd",      55),
]

# Number of shipments
n_items = len(shipments)

# Upper bound on the number of pallets needed = one pallet per shipment
# (can be tightened, but this bound is safe)
n_pallets = n_items

# Pallet capacity (kg)
CAPACITY = 100

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("PalletPacking", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
# x[(i,p)] = 1 if shipment i is placed on pallet p, else 0
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    ((i, p) for i in range(n_items) for p in range(n_pallets)),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# y[p] = 1 if pallet p is used, else 0
y = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "y",
    (p for p in range(n_pallets)),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# Objective: minimise the number of pallets used
model += pulp.lpSum(y[p] for p in range(n_pallets)), "MinNumberOfPallets"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Every shipment must be assigned to exactly one pallet
for i in range(n_items):
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, p)] for p in range(n_pallets)) == 1, f"AssignOnce_item_{i}"

# 2) Capacity of each pallet must not be exceeded
for p in range(n_pallets):
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(shipments[i][1] * x[(i, p)] for i in range(n_items))
        <= CAPACITY * y[p]
    ), f"Capacity_pallet_{p}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Solver status: {status}")

if status == "Optimal":
    used_pallets = [p for p in range(n_pallets) if pulp.value(y[p]) > 0.5]
    print(f"Minimum number of pallets required: {len(used_pallets)}\n")

    for p in used_pallets:
        assigned = [
            shipments[i][0] + f"({shipments[i][1]}kg)"
            for i in range(n_items)
            if pulp.value(x[(i, p)]) > 0.5
        ]
        total_weight = sum(shipments[i][1] for i in range(n_items) if pulp.value(x[(i, p)]) > 0.5)
        print(f"Pallet {p + 1} (total {total_weight} kg):")
        for s in assigned:
            print(f"  - {s}")
        print()
else:
    print("No optimal solution found.")

identical pallets (capacity = 100 kg) using PuLP and the HiGHS solver.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
items = [
    ("Alpha",   45),
    ("Beta",    41),
    ("Gamma",   45),
    ("Delta",   31),
    ("Epsilon", 40),
    ("Zeta",    65),
    ("Eta",     40),
    ("Theta",   35),
    ("Iota",    57),
    ("Kappa",   68),
    ("Lambda",  36),
    ("Mu",      69),
    ("Nu",      70),
    ("Xi",      59),
    ("Omicron", 39),
    ("Pi",      69),
    ("Rho",     68),
    ("Sigma",   32),
]

capacity = 100                     # pallet capacity (kg)
max_pallets = len(items)           # a trivial upper bound (one item per pallet)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Pallet_Minimisation", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
# y_k = 1 if pallet k is used, 0 otherwise
y = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("PalletUsed", (k for k in range(max_pallets)), cat=pulp.LpBinary)

# x_i_k = 1 if item i is placed on pallet k, 0 otherwise
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "Assign",
    ((i, k) for i in range(len(items)) for k in range(max_pallets)),
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# Objective: minimise the number of pallets used
model += pulp.lpSum(y[k] for k in range(max_pallets)), "MinPallets"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Every item must be assigned to exactly one pallet
for i in range(len(items)):
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, k)] for k in range(max_pallets)) == 1, f"AssignItem_{i}"

# 2) Capacity of each pallet must not be exceeded
for k in range(max_pallets):
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(items[i][1] * x[(i, k)] for i in range(len(items)))
        <= capacity * y[k]
    ), f"Capacity_{k}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Solver status: {status}")

if status == "Optimal":
    used_pallets = [k for k in range(max_pallets) if pulp.value(y[k]) > 0.5]
    print(f"Minimum number of pallets required: {len(used_pallets)}\n")

    # Build a readable assignment list
    assignments = {k: [] for k in used_pallets}
    for i, (name, weight) in enumerate(items):
        for k in used_pallets:
            if pulp.value(x[(i, k)]) > 0.5:
                assignments[k].append((name, weight))
                break

    for k in used_pallets:
        total = sum(w for (_, w) in assignments[k])
        print(f"Pallet {k + 1} (total {total} kg):")
        for name, w in assignments[k]:
            print(f"  - {name}: {w} kg")
        print()
else:
    print("No optimal solution found.")

Bin‑packing model for assigning fragile equipment modules to reinforced pallets.
Each pallet can carry at most 100 kg. The model minimizes the number of pallets used.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# module names and their masses (kg)
modules = {
    "Alpha":   33,
    "Beta":    54,
    "Gamma":   56,
    "Delta":   30,
    "Epsilon": 56,
    "Zeta":    50,
    "Eta":     58,
    "Theta":   43,
    "Iota":    53,
    "Kappa":   48,
    "Lambda":  60,
    "Mu":      35,
    "Nu":      41,
    "Xi":      36,
    "Omicron": 47,
}

# Upper bound on number of pallets = number of items (trivial feasible bound)
max_pallets = len(modules)          # 15

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Pallet_Loading_Min_Pallets", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
# x[(i,k)] = 1 if module i is placed on pallet k, else 0
x = {}
for i in modules:
    for k in range(max_pallets):
        x[(i, k)] = pulp.LpVariable(f"x_{i}_{k}", cat="Binary")

# y[k] = 1 if pallet k is used, else 0
y = {}
for k in range(max_pallets):
    y[k] = pulp.LpVariable(f"y_{k}", cat="Binary")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise number of pallets used
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += pulp.lpSum(y[k] for k in range(max_pallets)), "Total_Pallets"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Every module must be assigned to exactly one pallet
for i in modules:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, k)] for k in range(max_pallets)) == 1, f"Assign_{i}"

# 2) Capacity of each pallet must not exceed 100 kg
capacity = 100
for k in range(max_pallets):
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(modules[i] * x[(i, k)] for i in modules) <= capacity * y[k],
        f"Cap_{k}",
    )

# 3) Linking constraint (optional but strengthens formulation):
#    If a pallet is not used (y_k = 0) then no item can be assigned to it.
#    This is already enforced by the capacity constraint, but we add it
#    for clarity.
for k in range(max_pallets):
    for i in modules:
        model += x[(i, k)] <= y[k], f"Link_{i}_{k}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Solver status: {status}")

if status == "Optimal":
    # Determine which pallets are actually used
    used_pallets = [k for k in range(max_pallets) if pulp.value(y[k]) > 0.5]
    print(f"Minimum number of pallets required: {len(used_pallets)}\n")

    # Show the loading plan
    for k in used_pallets:
        assigned = [i for i in modules if pulp.value(x[(i, k)]) > 0.5]
        total_mass = sum(modules[i] for i in assigned)
        print(f"Pallet {k+1} (total {total_mass} kg): {', '.join(assigned)}")

    print("No optimal solution found.")

over a 19‑day horizon using PuLP (HiGHS solver).

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
planning_horizon = 19

# Daily demand (units)
demand = [
    37, 48, 35, 51, 26,
    53, 40, 50, 50, 48,
    60, 11, 32, 32, 59,
    60, 23, 54, 51
]

# Cost parameters
procurement_cost = 5      # per unit ordered
holding_cost     = 3      # per unit held overnight (end‑of‑day inventory)
shortage_cost    = 9      # per unit of unmet demand

# Storage capacity
capacity = 63

# Initial inventory (units)
initial_inventory = 4

# Order size limits (units) – must be between 6 and 48 inclusive
order_min = 6
order_max = 48

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("BloodBank_Procurement_and_Storage", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
# x[t]   : quantity ordered on day t (t = 1..19)
# I[t]   : inventory at the end of day t (t = 1..19)
# S[t]   : shortage (unmet demand) on day t (t = 1..19)
x = {}
I = {}
S = {}

for t in range(1, planning_horizon + 1):
    x[t] = pulp.LpVariable(f"x_{t}", lowBound=order_min, upBound=order_max, cat="Continuous")
    I[t] = pulp.LpVariable(f"I_{t}", lowBound=0, upBound=capacity, cat="Continuous")
    S[t] = pulp.LpVariable(f"S_{t}", lowBound=0, upBound=demand[t-1], cat="Continuous")  # shortage cannot exceed demand

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Inventory balance with 1‑day lead time.
# Shipments ordered on day t become available on day t+1.
# For day 1 there is no incoming shipment.
for t in range(1, planning_horizon + 1):
    if t == 1:
        # No receipt on day 1 (x_0 does not exist)
        model += (initial_inventory + 0 + S[t] == demand[t-1] + I[t],
                  f"balance_day_{t}")
    else:
        # Receipt on day t is the order placed on day t‑1
        model += (I[t-1] + x[t-1] + S[t] == demand[t-1] + I[t],
                  f"balance_day_{t}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective function
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
total_procurement = pulp.lpSum(procurement_cost * x[t] for t in range(1, planning_horizon + 1))
total_holding    = pulp.lpSum(holding_cost * I[t] for t in range(1, planning_horizon + 1))
total_shortage   = pulp.lpSum(shortage_cost * S[t] for t in range(1, planning_horizon + 1))

model += total_procurement + total_holding + total_shortage, "Total_Cost"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Solver status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Total cost: {pulp.value(model.objective):.2f}\n")

print("Day | Order (x) | End‑Inv (I) | Shortage (S)")
print("-" * 40)

    short   = S[t].varValue

# End of script

shortage_penalty_per_ml = 6  # $ per megalitre of unmet demand

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Water_Reservoir_Planning", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
pump = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("pump", days, lowBound=0, upBound=50, cat="Continuous")
pump_on = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("pump_on", days, cat="Binary")   # 1 if we pump on that day
shortage = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("shortage", days, lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")
storage = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("storage", days, lowBound=0, upBound=capacity, cat="Continuous")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

    model += pump[t] >= 8 * pump_on[t]          # if we pump, at least 8 ML
    model += pump[t] <= 50 * pump_on[t]         # if we pump, at most 50 ML
    # when pump_on[t] = 0, pump[t] is forced to 0

c_shortage = 7.0     # penalty per unit of unmet demand

# Model

model = pulp.LpProblem("Procurement_Storage_Planning", pulp.LpMinimize)

    "order", T, lowBound=procure_lb, upBound=procure_ub, cat=pulp.LpContinuous
)                      # quantity ordered on day t (arrives next day)

    "stock", T, lowBound=0.0, upBound=storage_capacity, cat=pulp.LpContinuous

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
days = 18

# Daily demand (index starts at 1 for readability)
demand = {
    1: 11, 2: 13, 3: 48, 4: 60, 5: 35, 6: 18,
    7: 45, 8: 56, 9: 55, 10: 29, 11: 36, 12: 35,
    13: 44, 14: 13, 15: 57, 16: 38, 17: 44, 18: 19
}

# Cost parameters
c_procure = 5   # per unit purchased
c_hold    = 1   # per unit held overnight (end‑of‑day inventory)
c_penalty = 7   # per unit of unmet demand (deficit)

# Storage capacity
capacity = 71

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Procurement_Storage_Planning", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
# Inventory at end of each day (including day 0 = initial stock)
I = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("Inv", range(0, days + 1), lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Deficit (lost demand) each day
L = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("Deficit", range(1, days + 1), lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Quantity ordered on day t (arrives start of day t+1). Orders on day 18 are useless,
# therefore we only create variables for t = 1 .. 17.
Q = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("Order", range(1, days), lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Binary indicator: 1 if an order is placed on day t, 0 otherwise
Y = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("OrderFlag", range(1, days), cat="Binary")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Initial condition
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += (I[0] == 71), "Initial_Inventory"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Order size constraints (4 ≤ Q_t ≤ 61 when an order is placed)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for t in range(1, days):
    model += (Q[t] >= 4 * Y[t]), f"MinOrder_day{t}"
    model += (Q[t] <= 61 * Y[t]), f"MaxOrder_day{t}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Inventory flow and deficit constraints
#   I_{t-1} + Q_{t-1} + L_t = D_t + I_t   for t = 1 .. 18
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for t in range(1, days + 1):
    prev_order = Q[t - 1] if (t - 1) >= 1 else 0  # Q_0 = 0
    model += (
        I[t - 1] + prev_order + L[t] == demand[t] + I[t]
    ), f"Flow_day{t}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Storage capacity constraints
#   (stock available before demand) ≤ capacity
#   End‑of‑day inventory ≤ capacity
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for t in range(1, days + 1):
    prev_order = Q[t - 1] if (t - 1) >= 1 else 0
    model += (I[t - 1] + prev_order <= capacity), f"Cap_preDemand_day{t}"
    model += (I[t] <= capacity), f"Cap_endDay_day{t}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimize total cost
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
total_cost = (
    c_procure * pulp.lpSum(Q[t] for t in range(1, days)) +
    c_hold    * pulp.lpSum(I[t] for t in range(1, days + 1)) +
    c_penalty * pulp.lpSum(L[t] for t in range(1, days + 1))
)

model += total_cost, "Total_Cost"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Total cost = {pulp.value(model.objective):.2f}\n")

print("Day | Order | OrderFlag | EndInv | Deficit")

over a 7‑day horizon.

Model:
    min  4 * Σ q_t            (procurement cost)
        + 2 * Σ I_t            (refrigeration cost)
        + 8 * Σ s_t            (shortage penalty)

         I_{t-1} + q_t - demand_t = I_t + s_t      (balance)
         0 ≤ I_t ≤ 33                               (capacity)
         0 ≤ s_t                                    (shortage non‑negative)
         1 ≤ q_t ≤ 39                               (order bounds)
         I_t , s_t , q_t continuous
"""

import pulp

# -----------------------------
# Data
# -----------------------------
days = range(1, 8)                     # 1 … 7
initial_stock = 16
capacity = 33

demand = {
    1: 40,
    2: 14,
    3: 15,
    4: 43,
    5: 12,
    6: 14,
    7: 24,
}

procurement_cost = 4
holding_cost = 2
shortage_cost = 8

# -----------------------------
# Model
# -----------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("BloodBank_WeeklyPlan", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
q = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("order", days, lowBound=1, upBound=39, cat="Continuous")
I = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("inventory", days, lowBound=0, upBound=capacity, cat="Continuous")
s = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("shortage", days, lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Objective
model += (
    procurement_cost * pulp.lpSum(q[t] for t in days)
    + holding_cost * pulp.lpSum(I[t] for t in days)
    + shortage_cost * pulp.lpSum(s[t] for t in days)
)

# Constraints
# Inventory balance constraints
for t in days:
    if t == 1:
        prev_inventory = initial_stock
    else:
        prev_inventory = I[t - 1]

    # I_{t-1} + q_t - demand_t = I_t + s_t
    model += (
        prev_inventory + q[t] - demand[t] == I[t] + s[t],
        f"balance_day_{t}"
    )

# -----------------------------
# Solve
# -----------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# -----------------------------
# Output
# -----------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Total cost = {pulp.value(model.objective):.2f}\n")

print("Day | Order (q) | End‑Inventory (I) | Shortage (s) | Cost components")
print("-" * 70)
for t in days:
    order = q[t].varValue
    inv   = I[t].varValue
    short = s[t].varValue
    proc_cost = procurement_cost * order
    hold_cost = holding_cost * inv
    short_cost = shortage_cost * short
    print(f"{t:3d} | {order:9.2f} | {inv:15.2f} | {short:11.2f} | "
          f"P:{proc_cost:5.2f} H:{hold_cost:5.2f} S:{short_cost:5.2f}")

# Verify capacity and order bounds
print("\nVerification:")
for t in days:
    assert 1 - 1e-5 <= q[t].varValue <= 39 + 1e-5, f"Order bound violated on day {t}"
    assert 0 - 1e-5 <= I[t].varValue <= capacity + 1e-5, f"Capacity violated on day {t}"
    assert s[t].varValue >= -1e-5, f"Negative shortage on day {t}"

order_max = 57                  # max order size when an order is placed

shortage_penalty = 15           # $ per barrel of unmet demand

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Additive_Replenishment", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
order = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("order",
                              T,
                              lowBound=0,
                              upBound=order_max,
                              cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

order_flag = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("order_flag",
                                   T,
                                   cat=pulp.LpBinary)

inventory = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("inventory",
                                  T,
                                  lowBound=0,
                                  upBound=capacity,
                                  cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

shortage = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("shortage",
                                 T,
                                 lowBound=0,
                                 upBound=None,
                                 cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# Linking order size and order flag (optional order)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
for t in T:
    model += order[t] >= order_min * order_flag[t], f"MinOrderIfFlag_{t}"
    model += order[t] <= order_max * order_flag[t], f"MaxOrderIfFlag_{t}"

# ------------------------------------------------------------

# ------------------------------------------------------------
for t in T:
    # arrivals on day t are orders placed two days earlier
    if t >= 3:
        arrivals = order[t - 2]
    else:
        arrivals = 0

    inv_prev = initial_inventory if t == 1 else inventory[t - 1]

    # inventory after meeting demand (or shortage) and receiving arrivals
    model += (inventory[t] ==
              inv_prev + arrivals - (demand[t] - shortage[t])
              ), f"Balance_{t}"

    # shortage cannot exceed demand of the day
    model += shortage[t] <= demand[t], f"ShortageUpperBound_{t}"

            order[(op_i, op_j)] = var

# 3.1 Precedence inside each truck

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Scheduling of 6 trucks on 6 hubs with sequence-dependent operations.
Goal: minimise the makespan (completion time of the last loading/unloading).
The model uses start‑time variables (continuous) and binary ordering variables
to enforce the single‑resource (hub) capacity.
"""

import pulp

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# trucks[t] = list of (hub, processing_time) in the required order
trucks = {
    1: [(5, 2), (6, 1), (1, 1), (2, 2), (4, 6), (3, 8)],
    2: [(3, 4), (1, 3), (4, 9), (2, 9), (6, 2), (5, 9)],
    3: [(2, 8), (1, 7), (6, 5), (3, 1), (4, 10), (5, 3)],
    4: [(4, 2), (2, 10), (6, 7), (3, 6), (1, 4), (5, 9)],
    5: [(4, 9), (1, 8), (6, 9), (3, 7), (5, 8), (2, 5)],
    6: [(2, 8), (6, 2), (3, 2), (1, 8), (5, 7), (4, 10)],
}

num_trucks = len(trucks)
ops = []                               # list of all operations
for t, seq in trucks.items():
    for idx, (hub, dur) in enumerate(seq):
        ops.append((t, idx, hub, dur))

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Truck_Hub_Scheduling", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: start time of each operation
s = {}
for t, idx, hub, dur in ops:
    s[(t, idx)] = pulp.LpVariable(f"s_{t}_{idx}", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Makespan
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Objective: minimise makespan
model += Cmax, "Minimise_makespan"

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1) Every operation must finish before the makespan
for t, idx, hub, dur in ops:
    model += s[(t, idx)] + dur <= Cmax, f"completion_{t}_{idx}"

# 2) Precedence constraints inside each truck (the given order must be respected)
for t, seq in trucks.items():
    for i in range(len(seq) - 1):
        dur_i = seq[i][1]
        model += (
            s[(t, i + 1)] >= s[(t, i)] + dur_i,
            f"precedence_truck{t}_op{i}_to_{i+1}",
        )

# 3) Hub capacity: at most one truck at a hub at any time.
#    Use binary ordering variables for each unordered pair of operations that share a hub.
M = 300  # big‑M, larger than the total possible horizon (211)
y = {}   # binary variables

# Build a dictionary: hub -> list of (t, idx, dur)
hub_ops = {}
for t, idx, hub, dur in ops:
    hub_ops.setdefault(hub, []).append((t, idx, dur))

# For each hub, create ordering binaries for each unordered pair
for hub, op_list in hub_ops.items():
    n = len(op_list)
    for i in range(n):
        t1, idx1, dur1 = op_list[i]
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            t2, idx2, dur2 = op_list[j]
            # binary variable: 1 if (t1,idx1) precedes (t2,idx2), 0 otherwise
            y[(t1, idx1, t2, idx2)] = pulp.LpVariable(
                f"y_{t1}_{idx1}_{t2}_{idx2}", cat="Binary"
            )
            # Either 1 precedes 2
            model += (
                s[(t1, idx1)] + dur1
                <= s[(t2, idx2)] + M * (1 - y[(t1, idx1, t2, idx2)]),
                f"hub{hub}_order1_{t1}_{idx1}_before_{t2}_{idx2}",
            )
            # Or 2 precedes 1
            model += (
                s[(t2, idx2)] + dur2
                <= s[(t1, idx1)] + M * y[(t1, idx1, t2, idx2)],
                f"hub{hub}_order2_{t2}_{idx2}_before_{t1}_{idx1}",
            )

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Optimal makespan: {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")
print("Start times (truck, operation index) -> start")
for t, idx in sorted(s.keys()):
    print(f"Truck {t}, op {idx}: start at {pulp.value(s[(t, idx)])}")

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Job‑shop scheduling model for the 6‑truck, 6‑hub problem.
Each truck must visit the six hubs in a fixed order; each visit requires a
non‑preemptive loading time.  No two trucks may occupy the same hub at the same
time.  The model minimizes the makespan (completion time of the last
operation) using PuLP and the HiGHS solver.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Trucks are indexed 0..5, operations (stops) 0..5.
# For each truck we store a list of (hub, processing_time) pairs.
# Hubs are numbered 0..5 corresponding to Hub1..Hub6.
trucks = [
    # Truck 1
    [(4, 2), (5, 1), (0, 1), (1, 2), (3, 6), (2, 8)],
    # Truck 2
    [(2, 4), (0, 3), (3, 9), (1, 9), (5, 2), (4, 9)],
    # Truck 3
    [(1, 8), (0, 7), (5, 5), (2, 1), (3,10), (4, 3)],
    # Truck 4
    [(3, 2), (1,10), (5, 7), (2, 6), (0, 4), (4, 9)],
    # Truck 5
    [(3, 9), (0, 8), (5, 9), (2, 7), (4, 8), (1, 5)],
    # Truck 6
    [(1, 8), (5, 2), (2, 2), (0, 8), (4, 7), (3,10)],
]

num_trucks = len(trucks)          # 6
ops_per_truck = len(trucks[0])    # 6
num_hubs = 6

# Upper bound for the schedule (big‑M).  Sum of all processing times is 211,
# we use a safe larger value.
M = 1000

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Truck_Hub_Scheduling", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables:
#   start[t,o]  – start time of operation o (0‑based) of truck t
#   Z          – makespan (maximum completion time)
start = {}
for t in range(num_trucks):
    for o in range(ops_per_truck):
        var_name = f"s_{t}_{o}"
        start[t, o] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

Z = pulp.LpVariable("makespan", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Binary variables to break ties on the same hub:
#   before[(t,o),(t2,o2)] = 1 if operation (t,o) finishes before (t2,o2) starts
before = {}
for t1 in range(num_trucks):
    for o1 in range(ops_per_truck):
        hub1 = trucks[t1][o1][0]
        for t2 in range(num_trucks):
            for o2 in range(ops_per_truck):
                if (t1, o1) >= (t2, o2):
                    # avoid duplicate pairs and self‑pair
                    continue
                hub2 = trucks[t2][o2][0]
                if hub1 == hub2:  # same hub → need ordering
                    var_name = f"b_{t1}_{o1}_{t2}_{o2}"
                    before[(t1, o1, t2, o2)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Minimize makespan
model += Z, "Minimize_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Makespan must be at least the completion time of every operation
for t in range(num_trucks):
    for o in range(ops_per_truck):
        proc = trucks[t][o][1]
        model += Z >= start[t, o] + proc, f"Makespan_ge_Comp_{t}_{o}"

# 2) Precedence constraints within each truck (fixed order)
for t in range(num_trucks):
    for o in range(ops_per_truck - 1):
        proc = trucks[t][o][1]
        model += start[t, o + 1] >= start[t, o] + proc, f"Precedence_{t}_{o}"

# 3) No‑overlap constraints on each hub using binary ordering variables
for (t1, o1, t2, o2), bvar in before.items():
    proc1 = trucks[t1][o1][1]
    proc2 = trucks[t2][o2][1]

    # (t1,o1) before (t2,o2)  -->  start2 >= start1 + proc1
    model += start[t2, o2] >= start[t1, o1] + proc1 - M * (1 - bvar), f"Disj1_{t1}_{o1}_{t2}_{o2}"
    # (t2,o2) before (t1,o1)  -->  start1 >= start2 + proc2
    model += start[t1, o1] >= start[t2, o2] + proc2 - M * bvar,       f"Disj2_{t1}_{o1}_{t2}_{o2}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Optimal makespan: {pulp.value(Z):.2f} time units\n")

print("Start times (truck, operation, hub, processing, start):")
for t in range(num_trucks):
    for o in range(ops_per_truck):
        hub, proc = trucks[t][o]
        print(f"Truck {t+1:1d}, Op {o+1:1d} (Hub{hub+1}, p={proc}) -> start = {pulp.value(start[t,o]):.2f}")

        p = processing_time[t][k]
        hub_ops[h].append((t, k, p))

# Upper bound for the big‑M (sum of all processing times)
M = sum(sum(processing_time[t][k] for k in range(ops_per_truck)) for t in range(n_trucks))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Truck_Hub_Scheduling", pulp.LpMinimize)

S = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("Start",
                          ((t, k) for t in range(n_trucks) for k in range(ops_per_truck)),
                          lowBound=0,
                          cat='Continuous')

# Makespan
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat='Continuous')

Y = {}

"""
Job‑shop model for the 6‑truck, 6‑hub delivery problem.
Each truck has a fixed ordered list of (hub, processing time) operations.
Only one truck can be at a hub at any time.
The model minimizes the makespan (total completion time).
Solved with PuLP + HiGHS.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# trucks[truck] = list of (hub, processing_time) in the required order
trucks = {
    1: [(5, 2), (6, 1), (1, 1), (2, 2), (4, 6), (3, 8)],
    2: [(3, 4), (1, 3), (4, 9), (2, 9), (6, 2), (5, 9)],
    3: [(2, 8), (1, 7), (6, 5), (3, 1), (4, 10), (5, 3)],
    4: [(4, 2), (2, 10), (6, 7), (3, 6), (1, 4), (5, 9)],
    5: [(4, 9), (1, 8), (6, 9), (3, 7), (5, 8), (2, 5)],
    6: [(2, 8), (6, 2), (3, 2), (1, 8), (5, 7), (4, 10)]
}

# number of trucks / hubs / operations per truck
T = 6
H = 6
K = 6

# store processing time for each (truck, step)
proc = {}
for i in range(1, T + 1):
    for k in range(1, K + 1):
        hub, p = trucks[i][k - 1]
        proc[(i, k)] = p

# large constant (greater than any possible makespan)
M = sum(proc.values())   # 211 in this instance

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Delivery_JobShop", pulp.LpMinimize)

# start time variables S_i_k  (continuous, >=0)
S = {(i, k): pulp.LpVariable(f"S_{i}_{k}", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")
     for i in range(1, T + 1) for k in range(1, K + 1)}

# makespan
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Precedence constraints inside each truck
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for i in range(1, T + 1):
    for k in range(1, K):
        model += (S[(i, k)] + proc[(i, k)] <= S[(i, k + 1)],
                  f"Prec_{i}_{k}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Disjunctive (resource) constraints – one truck per hub at a time
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# collect operations belonging to each hub
hub_ops = {h: [] for h in range(1, H + 1)}
for i in range(1, T + 1):
    for k in range(1, K + 1):
        hub = trucks[i][k - 1][0]
        hub_ops[hub].append((i, k))

# binary ordering variables Y_i_k_j_l  (1 if (i,k) precedes (j,l) on the shared hub)
Y = {}
for h in range(1, H + 1):
    ops = hub_ops[h]
    for idx1 in range(len(ops)):
        i, k = ops[idx1]
        for idx2 in range(idx1 + 1, len(ops)):
            j, l = ops[idx2]
            var = pulp.LpVariable(f"Y_{i}_{k}_{j}_{l}", cat="Binary")
            Y[(i, k, j, l)] = var

            # (i,k) before (j,l)  OR  (j,l) before (i,k)
            model += (S[(i, k)] + proc[(i, k)] <= S[(j, l)] + M * (1 - var),
                      f"Res_{i}_{k}_before_{j}_{l}_hub{h}")
            model += (S[(j, l)] + proc[(j, l)] <= S[(i, k)] + M * var,
                      f"Res_{j}_{l}_before_{i}_{k}_hub{h}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Makespan definition
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for i in range(1, T + 1):
    for k in range(1, K + 1):
        model += (S[(i, k)] + proc[(i, k)] <= Cmax,
                  f"Completion_{i}_{k}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise makespan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimize_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output (optional, can be omitted if only the script is required)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print("Status :", pulp.LpStatus[model.status])
print("Minimum makespan =", pulp.value(Cmax))
print("\nStart times (truck, step):")
for i in range(1, T + 1):
    for k in range(1, K + 1):
        print(f"Truck {i}, step {k} (Hub {trucks[i][k-1][0]}):  start = {pulp.value(S[(i,k)]):.2f}")

"""
Job‑shop model for the 6‑truck, 6‑hub scheduling problem.
Each truck follows a fixed ordered list of (hub, processing time) operations.
Only one truck can be at a hub at any time and each operation is non‑preemptive.
The model minimizes the makespan (completion of the last operation).

Solver: HiGHS via PuLP
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Trucks are indexed 0..5, operations inside each truck are indexed 0..5
# (hub, processing time) for each truck in the given order
truck_ops = [
    # Truck 1
    [(5, 2), (6, 1), (1, 1), (2, 2), (4, 6), (3, 8)],
    # Truck 2
    [(3, 4), (1, 3), (4, 9), (2, 9), (6, 2), (5, 9)],
    # Truck 3
    [(2, 8), (1, 7), (6, 5), (3, 1), (4,10), (5, 3)],
    # Truck 4
    [(4, 2), (2,10), (6, 7), (3, 6), (1, 4), (5, 9)],
    # Truck 5
    [(4, 9), (1, 8), (6, 9), (3, 7), (5, 8), (2, 5)],
    # Truck 6
    [(2, 8), (6, 2), (3, 2), (1, 8), (5, 7), (4,10)]
]

num_trucks = len(truck_ops)
ops_per_truck = len(truck_ops[0])          # all trucks have 6 operations
num_ops = num_trucks * ops_per_truck       # total number of operations = 36

# Create flat lists for easy indexing
hub = {}          # hub[(i,k)]  = hub number (1..6)
proc = {}         # proc[(i,k)] = processing time
for i in range(num_trucks):
    for k in range(ops_per_truck):
        hub[(i, k)] = truck_ops[i][k][0]
        proc[(i, k)] = truck_ops[i][k][1]

# Big‑M value – sum of all processing times is safe
M = sum(proc.values())

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Truck_Hub_Scheduling", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
# start time of each operation (continuous, >=0)
S = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("Start",
                          ((i, k) for i in range(num_trucks) for k in range(ops_per_truck)),
                          lowBound=0,
                          cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# makespan variable
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Makespan", lowBound=0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# Binary ordering variables for every pair of operations that share the same hub
Y = {}   # Y[(i,k,j,l)] = 1 if (i,k) is scheduled after (j,l) on the common hub
for i in range(num_trucks):
    for k in range(ops_per_truck):
        for j in range(num_trucks):
            for l in range(ops_per_truck):
                if (i, k) < (j, l):          # consider each unordered pair once
                    if hub[(i, k)] == hub[(j, l)]:
                        Y[(i, k, j, l)] = pulp.LpVariable(
                            f"Y_{i}_{k}_{j}_{l}", cat=pulp.LpBinary)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise makespan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimise makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Completion of each operation must be before makespan
for i in range(num_trucks):
    for k in range(ops_per_truck):
        model += S[(i, k)] + proc[(i, k)] <= Cmax, f"Makespan_bound_{i}_{k}"

# 2) Precedence constraints inside each truck (job order)
for i in range(num_trucks):
    for k in range(ops_per_truck - 1):
        model += S[(i, k + 1)] >= S[(i, k)] + proc[(i, k)], f"Precedence_{i}_{k}"

# 3) Disjunctive (resource) constraints for each hub
for (i, k, j, l), y_var in Y.items():
    # (i,k) after (j,l)  -->  S_ik >= S_jl + p_jl  - M*(1 - y)
    model += S[(i, k)] >= S[(j, l)] + proc[(j, l)] - M * (1 - y_var), \
             f"HubSeq1_{i}_{k}_{j}_{l}"
    # (j,l) after (i,k)  -->  S_jl >= S_ik + p_ik  - M*y
    model += S[(j, l)] >= S[(i, k)] + proc[(i, k)] - M * y_var, \
             f"HubSeq2_{i}_{k}_{j}_{l}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output results
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Optimal makespan: {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

# Gather schedule sorted by start time for readability
schedule = []
for i in range(num_trucks):
    for k in range(ops_per_truck):
        start = pulp.value(S[(i, k)])
        schedule.append((start, i + 1, k + 1, hub[(i, k)], proc[(i, k)]))

schedule.sort()
print("Start  Truck  Op  Hub  Proc")
for st, tr, op, h, p in schedule:
    print(f"{st:5.1f}   {tr:2d}    {op:2d}   {h:2d}   {p:2d}")

Only one truck can be loading at a hub at any time.

    [(2, 8), (1, 7), (6, 5), (3, 1), (4,10), (5, 3)],   # Truck 3
    [(4, 2), (2,10), (6, 7), (3, 6), (1, 4), (5, 9)],   # Truck 4
    [(4, 9), (1, 8), (6, 9), (3, 7), (5, 8), (2, 5)],   # Truck 5
    [(2, 8), (6, 2), (3, 2), (1, 8), (5, 7), (4,10)],   # Truck 6
]

num_trucks = len(truck_routes)          # 6
num_ops_per_truck = len(truck_routes[0]) # 6 (all trucks have the same length)

# Convert hub numbers from the statement (Hub1‑6) to 0‑based indices
def hub_to_idx(h):
    return h - 1

# Build structures:
#   proc[i][k]  = processing time of operation k of truck i
#   hub_of[i][k] = hub index of that operation
proc = {}
hub_of = {}
for i, route in enumerate(truck_routes):
    for k, (h_raw, p) in enumerate(route):
        h = hub_to_idx(h_raw)
        proc[(i, k)] = p
        hub_of[(i, k)] = h

# For each hub, list the (truck, operation_index, processing_time) that uses it
ops_at_hub = {h: [] for h in range(6)}

    for k in range(num_ops_per_truck):

        ops_at_hub[h].append((i, k, proc[(i, k)]))

M = sum(proc.values())

)

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Scheduling of 6 trucks at 6 hubs.
Each truck must follow its fixed route (hub, processing time) in order.
Only one truck can be at a hub at a time.
Goal: minimise the makespan (completion time of the last loading).
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# truck_id : list of (hub, processing_time) in the required order
trucks = {
    1: [(5, 2), (6, 1), (1, 1), (2, 2), (4, 6), (3, 8)],
    2: [(3, 4), (1, 3), (4, 9), (2, 9), (6, 2), (5, 9)],
    3: [(2, 8), (1, 7), (6, 5), (3, 1), (4,10), (5, 3)],
    4: [(4, 2), (2,10), (6, 7), (3, 6), (1, 4), (5, 9)],
    5: [(4, 9), (1, 8), (6, 9), (3, 7), (5, 8), (2, 5)],
    6: [(2, 8), (6, 2), (3, 2), (1, 8), (5, 7), (4,10)],
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Indexing of operations
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# each operation is identified by a tuple (truck, step) where step = 0..5
ops = []                                   # list of all operation identifiers
proc_time = {}                             # processing time of each operation
hub_of = {}                                # hub required by each operation
for t, seq in trucks.items():
    for k, (h, p) in enumerate(seq):
        op = (t, k)
        ops.append(op)
        proc_time[op] = p
        hub_of[op] = h

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper structures
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# operations grouped by hub (for disjunctive constraints)
ops_by_hub = {}
for op in ops:
    h = hub_of[op]
    ops_by_hub.setdefault(h, []).append(op)

# big-M – a horizon larger than any feasible makespan
M = sum(proc_time.values()) + 10   # safe upper bound

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Truck_Hub_Scheduling", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
# start time of each operation (continuous, >=0)
start = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("Start", ops, lowBound=0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# binary ordering variables for every pair of operations that share a hub
order = {}
for h, oplist in ops_by_hub.items():
    # consider each unordered pair once
    for i in range(len(oplist)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(oplist)):
            o1 = oplist[i]
            o2 = oplist[j]
            # y_{o1,o2} = 1  => o1 finishes before o2 starts
            var = pulp.LpVariable(f"Y_{o1}_{o2}", cat=pulp.LpBinary)
            order[(o1, o2)] = var

# makespan variable
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimise_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) precedence inside each truck (must follow given order)
for t, seq in trucks.items():
    for k in range(len(seq) - 1):
        o_curr = (t, k)
        o_next = (t, k + 1)
        model += (
            start[o_next] >= start[o_curr] + proc_time[o_curr],
            f"Truck_{t}_order_{k}_to_{k+1}",
        )

# 2) non‑overlap at each hub using binary ordering variables
for (o1, o2), y in order.items():
    # o1 before o2
    model += (
        start[o1] + proc_time[o1] <= start[o2] + M * (1 - y),
        f"Hub_{hub_of[o1]}_{o1}_before_{o2}",
    )
    # o2 before o1
    model += (
        start[o2] + proc_time[o2] <= start[o1] + M * y,
        f"Hub_{hub_of[o2]}_{o2}_before_{o1}",
    )

# 3) definition of makespan
for t in trucks.keys():
    last_op = (t, len(trucks[t]) - 1)
    model += (
        Cmax >= start[last_op] + proc_time[last_op],
        f"Makespan_def_truck_{t}",
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Minimum makespan = {pulp.value(Cmax):.2f} time units\n")

print("Start times (Truck, Step) -> (Hub, Start, Duration, Finish):")
for t in sorted(trucks.keys()):
    for k, (h, p) in enumerate(trucks[t]):
        op = (t, k)
        s = pulp.value(start[op])
        f = s + p
        print(f"  Truck {t}, step {k+1} (Hub {h}): start={s:.2f}, dur={p}, finish={f:.2f}")

# -----------------------------
# Jobs (shipments) are numbered 1..5, operations within each job are indexed 0..4
# Each operation is a tuple (hub, processing_time)

jobs = {
    1: [(5, 8), (4, 7), (1, 4), (2, 8), (3, 8)],
    2: [(5, 5), (3, 3), (2, 8), (1, 1), (4,10)],
    3: [(2, 1), (1, 9), (5, 2), (3, 2), (4, 7)],
    4: [(1, 5), (3, 5), (5, 4), (4, 3), (2,10)],
    5: [(3, 6), (2, 7), (1, 3), (4, 6), (5, 7)],
}

# list of all operations with their attributes
ops = {}                     # key: (job, op_index) -> dict with 'machine' and 'proc'
all_proc_times = []         # used for big-M

for j, seq in jobs.items():
    for k, (hub, p) in enumerate(seq):
        ops[(j, k)] = {'machine': hub, 'proc': p}
        all_proc_times.append(p)

# Big M (larger than any possible makespan)
M = sum(all_proc_times) + 1   # 140 is safe (total 139)

# -----------------------------
# Model
# -----------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Logistics_JobShop", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: start time of each operation
start = {}
for (j, k) in ops:
    start[(j, k)] = pulp.LpVariable(f"start_{j}_{k}", lowBound=0, cat='Continuous')

# Makespan variable
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat='Continuous')

# Objective: minimise makespan
model += Cmax, "Minimise_makespan"

# ---- 1) Precedence constraints within each job ----
for j, seq in jobs.items():
    for k in range(len(seq) - 1):
        model += (
            start[(j, k + 1)] >= start[(j, k)] + ops[(j, k)]['proc'],
            f"Job_{j}_precedence_{k}"
        )

# ---- 2) Disjunctive (machine capacity) constraints ----
# For each hub, collect the operations that require it
hub_to_ops = {}
for (j, k), attr in ops.items():
    hub = attr['machine']
    hub_to_ops.setdefault(hub, []).append((j, k))

# Binary ordering variables for each unordered pair of ops on the same hub
y = {}
for hub, op_list in hub_to_ops.items():
    # create constraints for every unordered pair
    for i in range(len(op_list)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(op_list)):
            op_a = op_list[i]
            op_b = op_list[j]
            # binary variable: 1 if a precedes b, 0 otherwise
            y[(op_a, op_b)] = pulp.LpVariable(
                f"y_{op_a[0]}_{op_a[1]}_before_{op_b[0]}_{op_b[1]}", cat='Binary'
            )
            p_a = ops[op_a]['proc']
            p_b = ops[op_b]['proc']

            # a finishes before b starts   (if y = 1)
            model += (
                start[op_a] + p_a <= start[op_b] + M * (1 - y[(op_a, op_b)]),
                f"Hub_{hub}_order1_{op_a}_{op_b}"
            )
            # b finishes before a starts   (if y = 0)
            model += (
                start[op_b] + p_b <= start[op_a] + M * y[(op_a, op_b)],
                f"Hub_{hub}_order2_{op_a}_{op_b}"
            )

# ---- 3) Makespan definition ----
for j in jobs:
    last_k = len(jobs[j]) - 1
    model += (
        start[(j, last_k)] + ops[(j, last_k)]['proc'] <= Cmax,
        f"Makespan_job_{j}"
    )

# -----------------------------
# Solve
# -----------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# -----------------------------
# Output (optional, can be removed if not needed)
# -----------------------------
print("Status:", pulp.LpStatus[model.status])
print("Minimum total completion time (makespan):", pulp.value(Cmax))
print("\nStart times:")

          f"proc {ops[(j,k)]['proc']}h) -> start at {pulp.value(start[(j,k)]):.2f}")

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Job‑shop scheduling model for 5 shipments (jobs) and 5 hubs (machines).
Each shipment follows a fixed order of hubs; each hub can handle only one shipment at a time.
The model minimizes the makespan (total completion time) using PuLP with the HiGHS solver.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
jobs = ["S1", "S2", "S3", "S4", "S5"]
machines = ["H1", "H2", "H3", "H4", "H5"]

# Route for each shipment: ordered list of (hub, processing time)
route = {
    "S1": [("H5", 8), ("H4", 7), ("H1", 4), ("H2", 8), ("H3", 8)],
    "S2": [("H5", 5), ("H3", 3), ("H2", 8), ("H1", 1), ("H4", 10)],
    "S3": [("H2", 1), ("H1", 9), ("H5", 2), ("H3", 2), ("H4", 7)],
    "S4": [("H1", 5), ("H3", 5), ("H5", 4), ("H4", 3), ("H2", 10)],
    "S5": [("H3", 6), ("H2", 7), ("H1", 3), ("H4", 6), ("H5", 7)],
}

# Helper dictionaries
proc_time = {}          # proc_time[(job, op_index)] = processing time
job_hub_index = {}      # job_hub_index[(job, hub)] = op_index (unique because each hub appears once per job)

for j in jobs:
    for idx, (h, p) in enumerate(route[j]):
        proc_time[(j, idx)] = p
        job_hub_index[(j, h)] = idx

# Big‑M: a safe upper bound on any start‑time difference
M = sum(p for p in proc_time.values()) + 10   # 10 extra slack

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Logistics_JobShop", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
#   start[(j, k)] : start time of operation k of job j (continuous, >=0)
start = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "Start",
    [(j, k) for j in jobs for k in range(5)],
    lowBound=0,
    cat="Continuous"
)

#   y[(i, j, h)] : binary = 1 if job i precedes job j on hub h
y = {}
for h in machines:
    for i_idx in range(len(jobs)):
        for j_idx in range(i_idx + 1, len(jobs)):
            i = jobs[i_idx]
            j = jobs[j_idx]
            var_name = f"Y_{i}_{j}_{h}"
            y[(i, j, h)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")

# Makespan
C_max = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += C_max, "Minimize_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Precedence constraints inside each job (fixed processing order)
for j in jobs:
    for k in range(4):  # 0..3, each operation must finish before the next starts
        model += (
            start[(j, k + 1)] >= start[(j, k)] + proc_time[(j, k)],
            f"Precedence_{j}_op{k}_to_{k+1}"
        )

# 2) Disjunctive (machine capacity) constraints: one job at a time per hub
for h in machines:
    # collect the operation index of each job on hub h
    op_index = {j: job_hub_index[(j, h)] for j in jobs}
    for i_idx in range(len(jobs)):
        for j_idx in range(i_idx + 1, len(jobs)):
            i = jobs[i_idx]
            j = jobs[j_idx]
            ki = op_index[i]
            kj = op_index[j]
            pi = proc_time[(i, ki)]
            pj = proc_time[(j, kj)]
            # i before j on hub h
            model += (
                start[(i, ki)] + pi <= start[(j, kj)] + M * (1 - y[(i, j, h)]),
                f"Machine_{h}_{i}_before_{j}"
            )
            # j before i on hub h
            model += (
                start[(j, kj)] + pj <= start[(i, ki)] + M * y[(i, j, h)],
                f"Machine_{h}_{j}_before_{i}"
            )

# 3) Makespan must be at least each job's completion time
for j in jobs:
    last_op = 4
    model += (
        C_max >= start[(j, last_op)] + proc_time[(j, last_op)],
        f"Makespan_bound_{j}"
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# (Optional) Print results – can be removed if only the script is required
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
if pulp.LpStatus[model.status] == "Optimal":
    print("Optimal makespan:", pulp.value(C_max))
    for j in jobs:
        print(f"\nSchedule for {j}:")
        for k, (h, _) in enumerate(route[j]):
            st = pulp.value(start[(j, k)])
            pt = proc_time[(j, k)]
            print(f"  Operation {k+1} on {h}: start = {st:.2f}, finish = {st + pt:.2f}")
else:
    print("No optimal solution found. Status:", pulp.LpStatus[model.status])

"""
Job‑shop model for the 5 shipments / 5 hubs problem.
Each shipment must follow its given sequence of hub‑operations.
The model minimizes the makespan (completion time of the last shipment).

Solver: HiGHS via PuLP
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# shipments : list of (hub, processing time) in the required order
shipments = {
    1: [(5, 8), (4, 7), (1, 4), (2, 8), (3, 8)],
    2: [(5, 5), (3, 3), (2, 8), (1, 1), (4,10)],
    3: [(2, 1), (1, 9), (5, 2), (3, 2), (4, 7)],
    4: [(1, 5), (3, 5), (5, 4), (4, 3), (2,10)],
    5: [(3, 6), (2, 7), (1, 3), (4, 6), (5, 7)]
}

num_shipments = len(shipments)          # =5
ops_per_shipment = 5                    # each shipment has exactly 5 operations

# big‑M – a number larger than any possible makespan
M = 200

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Logistics_JobShop", pulp.LpMinimize)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.1 Decision variables
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# start time of operation (s, o)  – continuous, >=0
start = {}
for s, ops in shipments.items():
    for o in range(ops_per_shipment):
        var_name = f"start_s{s}_o{o}"
        start[(s, o)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# makespan variable
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# binary ordering variables for every pair of operations that use the same hub
# y[(i),(j)] = 1  ⇒ operation i finishes before operation j starts
order = {}

# Helper: collect all operations with their hub and processing time
# each operation gets a unique id = (s, o)
op_data = {}
for s, ops in shipments.items():
    for o, (hub, p) in enumerate(ops):
        op_data[(s, o)] = {"hub": hub, "proc": p}

# Build ordering binaries for each hub
for hub in range(1, 6):                     # hubs are 1..5
    # list of operations that run on this hub
    ops_on_hub = [op for op, d in op_data.items() if d["hub"] == hub]
    # create binary for each unordered pair
    for i in range(len(ops_on_hub)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(ops_on_hub)):
            op_i = ops_on_hub[i]
            op_j = ops_on_hub[j]
            var_name = f"y_{op_i[0]}_{op_i[1]}_before_{op_j[0]}_{op_j[1]}"
            order[(op_i, op_j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.2 Objective
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimize_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.3 Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2.3.1 Job‑precedence constraints (each shipment follows its given order)
for s, ops in shipments.items():
    for o in range(ops_per_shipment - 1):
        p = ops[o][1]  # processing time of operation o
        model += (start[(s, o + 1)] >= start[(s, o)] + p,
                  f"precedence_s{s}_o{o}")

# 2.3.2 Disjunctive (no‑overlap) constraints on each hub
for (i, j), y_ij in order.items():
    p_i = op_data[i]["proc"]
    p_j = op_data[j]["proc"]
    # i before j  (y_ij = 1)  -> start_i + p_i <= start_j
    model += (start[i] + p_i <= start[j] + M * (1 - y_ij),
              f"no_overlap_{i}_before_{j}")
    # j before i  (y_ij = 0)  -> start_j + p_j <= start_i
    model += (start[j] + p_j <= start[i] + M * y_ij,
              f"no_overlap_{j}_before_{i}")

# 2.3.3 Definition of makespan
for s, ops in shipments.items():
    last_op = ops_per_shipment - 1
    p_last = ops[last_op][1]
    model += (Cmax >= start[(s, last_op)] + p_last,
              f"makespan_def_s{s}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Optimal makespan (Cmax): {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times (in hours):")
for s in range(1, num_shipments + 1):
    print(f"  Shipment {s}:")
    for o in range(ops_per_shipment):
        st = pulp.value(start[(s, o)])
        hub, proc = shipments[s][o]
        print(f"    Op {o+1} (Hub {hub}, {proc}h) -> start @ {st:.2f}")

op_info = {}
# hub -> list of operation identifiers that use this hub
hub_ops = {}

for s, ops in shipments.items():
    for idx, (hub, p) in enumerate(ops):
        op_id = (s, idx)                     # operation identifier
        op_info[op_id] = (hub, p)

        hub_ops.setdefault(hub, []).append(op_id)

# Upper bound M (big‑M) – sum of all processing times is sufficient
M = sum(p for ops in shipments.values() for (_, p) in ops)

# Model
# ------------------------------------------------------------------

start = {
    op_id: pulp.LpVariable(f"start_{op_id[0]}_{op_id[1]}", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")
    for op_id in op_info
}

# Binary ordering variables for every unordered pair that shares a hub
y = {}
for hub, ops in hub_ops.items():
    for i in range(len(ops)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(ops)):
            op_i = ops[i]
            op_j = ops[j]
            var_name = f"y_{op_i[0]}_{op_i[1]}_{op_j[0]}_{op_j[1]}"
            y[(op_i, op_j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")

# Makespan variable

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise makespan
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimise_makespan"

# 1) Precedence constraints inside each shipment
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
for s, ops in shipments.items():
    for k in range(len(ops) - 1):
        op_cur = (s, k)
        op_nxt = (s, k + 1)
        p_cur = op_info[op_cur][1]
        model += (
            start[op_cur] + p_cur <= start[op_nxt],
            f"precedence_{s}_{k}_to_{k+1}",

                f"hub_{hub}_order1_{op_i}_{op_j}",
