# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Job‑shop scheduling model for 4 delivery routes (jobs) and 4 distribution
centers (machines).  The model minimizes the makespan (total completion
time) using PuLP with the HiGHS solver.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
jobs = ["R1", "R2", "R3", "R4"]
machines = ["C1", "C2", "C3", "C4"]

# (job, operation index) -> (machine, processing time)
proc = {
    ("R1", 1): ("C3", 10), ("R1", 2): ("C2", 1), ("R1", 3): ("C1", 1), ("R1", 4): ("C4", 5),
    ("R2", 1): ("C2", 7),  ("R2", 2): ("C1", 9), ("R2", 3): ("C4", 3), ("R2", 4): ("C3", 5),
    ("R3", 1): ("C1", 5),  ("R3", 2): ("C2", 3), ("R3", 3): ("C4", 9), ("R3", 4): ("C3", 2),
    ("R4", 1): ("C3", 7),  ("R4", 2): ("C2", 2), ("R4", 3): ("C4", 2), ("R4", 4): ("C1", 9),
}

# Big‑M – larger than any feasible makespan
M = sum(p for (_, p) in proc.values())

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("DeliveryRouteScheduling", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: start time of each operation (continuous, >=0)
S = {}
for (j, o) in proc:
    var = pulp.LpVariable(f"S_{j}_{o}", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")
    S[(j, o)] = var

# Makespan variable (continuous, >=0)
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Binary ordering variables for every unordered pair of operations that share a machine
Y = {}
for m in machines:
    # collect all operations processed on machine m
    ops_on_m = [(j, o) for (j, o), (mc, _) in proc.items() if mc == m]
    # create binary variable for each unordered pair
    for i in range(len(ops_on_m)):
        for k in range(i + 1, len(ops_on_m)):
            op_i = ops_on_m[i]
            op_k = ops_on_m[k]
            y = pulp.LpVariable(f"Y_{op_i[0]}_{op_i[1]}_before_{op_k[0]}_{op_k[1]}", cat="Binary")
            Y[(op_i, op_k)] = y
            # also store the reverse key for convenience (will refer to same variable)
            Y[(op_k, op_i)] = y

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimize makespan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimize_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Job precedence constraints (operations within each route must follow given order)
for j in jobs:
    for o in range(1, 4):  # 1..3, because each job has 4 operations
        mc, p = proc[(j, o)]
        model += S[(j, o)] + p <= S[(j, o + 1)], f"Precedence_{j}_op{o}_to_{o+1}"

# 2) Machine capacity constraints using binary ordering variables
for m in machines:
    ops_on_m = [(j, o) for (j, o), (mc, _) in proc.items() if mc == m]
    for i in range(len(ops_on_m)):
        for k in range(i + 1, len(ops_on_m)):
            op_i = ops_on_m[i]
            op_k = ops_on_m[k]
            y = Y[(op_i, op_k)]

            # processing times
            pi = proc[op_i][1]
            pk = proc[op_k][1]

            # If y == 1 then op_i precedes op_k, else op_k precedes op_i
            model += S[op_i] + pi <= S[op_k] + M * (1 - y), f"Machine_{m}_{op_i}_before_{op_k}"
            model += S[op_k] + pk <= S[op_i] + M * y,       f"Machine_{m}_{op_k}_before_{op_i}"

# 3) Makespan must be at least the completion time of every operation
for (j, o), (_, p) in proc.items():
    model += S[(j, o)] + p <= Cmax, f"Makespan_{j}_{o}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Minimum makespan (total completion time): {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times of each handling stage:")
for (j, o) in sorted(S):
    start = pulp.value(S[(j, o)])
    mc, p = proc[(j, o)]
    print(f"  {j} – operation {o} (center {mc}, duration {p}): start at {start:.2f}")

print("\nOrdering decisions (for verification):")
for (op_a, op_b), yvar in Y.items():
    # print each unordered pair only once
    if op_a < op_b:
        order = "before" if pulp.value(yvar) > 0.5 else "after"
        print(f"  {op_a} is {order} {op_b}")

model += Cmax, "Minimize_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Precedence constraints (route order)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for r in [1, 2, 3, 4]:
    for o in [1, 2, 3]:  # each route has 4 stages, so 3 precedence links
        i = op_index[(r, o)]
        j = op_index[(r, o + 1)]
        p_i = ops[i][3]
        model += start[j] >= start[i] + p_i, f"Prec_R{r}_O{o}_to_O{o+1}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Disjunctive (machine) constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# For each center, collect operations that use it
center_ops = {}
for idx, (_, _, center, _) in enumerate(ops):
    center_ops.setdefault(center, []).append(idx)

# Binary variables: y[i,j] = 1 if operation i finishes before j starts
y = {}
for center, idx_list in center_ops.items():
    n = len(idx_list)
    for a in range(n):
        for b in range(a + 1, n):
            i = idx_list[a]
            j = idx_list[b]
            var_name = f"y_{i}_{j}"
            y[(i, j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat=pulp.LpBinary)

            p_i = ops[i][3]
            p_j = ops[j][3]

            # i before j  OR  j before i
            model += (
                start[i] + p_i <= start[j] + M * (1 - y[(i, j)]),
                f"Disj_{center}_i{i}_j{j}_1",
            )
            model += (
                start[j] + p_j <= start[i] + M * y[(i, j)],
                f"Disj_{center}_i{i}_j{j}_2",
            )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Makespan definition
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for i, (_, _, _, p) in enumerate(ops):
    model += Cmax >= start[i] + p, f"Makespan_op_{i}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print("Status:", pulp.LpStatus[model.status])
print("Minimum makespan:", pulp.value(Cmax))
print("\nStart times:")
for i, (r, o, c, p) in enumerate(ops):

        f"Route {r} – Stage {o} (Center {c}, dur {p}): start = {pulp.value(start[i]):.2f}"
    )

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Job‑shop model for the 4 delivery routes (R1‑R4) and 4 distribution centres (C1‑C4).

Each stage (operation) is denoted by (route, index) and has a fixed processing time
on a specific centre (machine).  The model minimizes the makespan (total
completion time) while respecting:
    • precedence of stages inside each route,
    • the fact that a centre can handle only one stage at a time (disjunctive
      constraints modelled with binary variables),
    • non‑preemptive processing (each stage runs continuously once started).

The formulation uses continuous start‑time variables, binary ordering variables
and a continuous makespan variable.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Operations: (route, stage) -> (centre, processing time)
ops = {
    ("R1", 1): ("C3", 10), ("R1", 2): ("C2", 1), ("R1", 3): ("C1", 1), ("R1", 4): ("C4", 5),
    ("R2", 1): ("C2", 7),  ("R2", 2): ("C1", 9), ("R2", 3): ("C4", 3), ("R2", 4): ("C3", 5),
    ("R3", 1): ("C1", 5),  ("R3", 2): ("C2", 3), ("R3", 3): ("C4", 9), ("R3", 4): ("C3", 2),
    ("R4", 1): ("C3", 7),  ("R4", 2): ("C2", 2), ("R4", 3): ("C4", 2), ("R4", 4): ("C1", 9)
}

# List of all operations
all_ops = list(ops.keys())

# Precedence constraints inside each route (stage i before i+1)
precedence = []
for r in ["R1", "R2", "R3", "R4"]:
    for k in range(1, 4):          # stages 1‑3 have a successor
        precedence.append(((r, k), (r, k + 1)))

# Group operations by centre (machine)
machine_ops = {}
for op, (machine, _) in ops.items():
    machine_ops.setdefault(machine, []).append(op)

# Big‑M value – larger than any possible makespan
M = 100

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Delivery_Routes_JobShop", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Continuous start time for each operation
start = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "Start",
    all_ops,
    lowBound=0,
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous
)

# Makespan variable
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# Binary ordering variables for each unordered pair of ops that share a centre
order = {}
for machine, oplist in machine_ops.items():
    # consider each unordered pair (i, j) with i < j (lexicographic order)
    for i in range(len(oplist)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(oplist)):
            op_i = oplist[i]
            op_j = oplist[j]
            var_name = f"Y_{op_i[0]}{op_i[1]}_before_{op_j[0]}{op_j[1]}"
            order[(op_i, op_j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat=pulp.LpBinary)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimize_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Precedence inside each route
for (prev, succ) in precedence:
    p_prev = ops[prev][1]
    model += (
        start[succ] >= start[prev] + p_prev,
        f"Precedence_{prev}_before_{succ}"
    )

# 2) Disjunctive constraints on each centre (machine)
for (op_i, op_j), y_ij in order.items():
    p_i = ops[op_i][1]
    p_j = ops[op_j][1]

    # i precedes j  =>  start_j >= start_i + p_i
    model += (
        start[op_j] >= start[op_i] + p_i - M * (1 - y_ij),
        f"Machine_{ops[op_i][0]}_{op_i}_before_{op_j}"
    )
    # j precedes i  =>  start_i >= start_j + p_j
    model += (
        start[op_i] >= start[op_j] + p_j - M * y_ij,
        f"Machine_{ops[op_i][0]}_{op_j}_before_{op_i}"
    )

# 3) Definition of makespan
for op in all_ops:
    p = ops[op][1]
    model += (
        Cmax >= start[op] + p,
        f"Makespan_def_{op}"
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Minimum makespan: {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times (in the optimal schedule):")
for op in sorted(all_ops):
    st = pulp.value(start[op])
    machine, proc = ops[op]
    print(f"  {op[0]} stage {op[1]} on {machine} (p={proc}) : start = {st:.2f}")

# optional: show ordering decisions for verification
print("\nOrdering decisions on each centre:")
for machine, oplist in machine_ops.items():
    print(f"  Centre {machine}:")
    for i in range(len(oplist)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(oplist)):
            op_i, op_j = oplist[i], oplist[j]
            y_val = pulp.value(order[(op_i, op_j)])
            if y_val is None:
                continue
            if y_val > 0.5:
                print(f"    {op_i[0]} stage {op_i[1]}  -->  {op_j[0]} stage {op_j[1]}")
            else:
                print(f"    {op_j[0]} stage {op_j[1]}  -->  {op_i[0]} stage {op_i[1]}")

    13: ("R4", 2, "C2",  2),
    14: ("R4", 3, "C4",  2),
    15: ("R4", 4, "C1",  9),
}

proc_time = {i: ops[i][3] for i in ops}
machine   = {i: ops[i][2] for i in ops}
route_ops = {
    "R1": [0, 1, 2, 3],
    "R2": [4, 5, 6, 7],
    "R3": [8, 9,10,11],
    "R4": [12,13,14,15],
}

# Big‑M (larger than any possible makespan)
M = sum(proc_time.values())   # 80

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Delivery_Route_Scheduling", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: start times (continuous) and ordering binaries (0/1)
start = {i: pulp.LpVariable(f"start_{i}", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")
         for i in ops}

# binary variables y_{i,j} for each unordered pair of operations that share a centre
y = {}
for i in ops:
    for j in ops:
        if i < j and machine[i] == machine[j]:
            y[(i, j)] = pulp.LpVariable(f"y_{i}_{j}", cat="Binary")

# Makespan variable
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimize_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Completion of each operation must be ≤ Cmax
for i in ops:
    model += start[i] + proc_time[i] <= Cmax, f"cmax_bound_{i}"

"""
Job‑shop model for the 6‑truck, 6‑center problem.
Solved with PuLP + HiGHS.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Routes: list of (center, handling time) for each truck (T1 … T6)
routes = {
    1: [("C5", 8), ("C2", 8), ("C4", 5), ("C1", 1), ("C3", 4), ("C6", 9)],
    2: [("C6", 2), ("C2", 5), ("C4", 3), ("C3",10), ("C5", 7), ("C1", 4)],
    3: [("C3", 6), ("C6", 4), ("C4", 6), ("C1", 8), ("C5", 4), ("C2", 5)],
    4: [("C3", 3), ("C2", 6), ("C6", 1), ("C1", 8), ("C5", 1), ("C4", 1)],
    5: [("C2", 1), ("C1", 6), ("C5", 7), ("C4", 3), ("C6", 4), ("C3", 8)],
    6: [("C4", 7), ("C2", 7), ("C3", 1), ("C5", 7), ("C1", 5), ("C6", 9)],
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create operation index and store attributes
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# op_key = (truck_id, position_in_route)   position starts at 0
ops = {}
total_proc_time = 0
for t, seq in routes.items():
    for pos, (center, proc) in enumerate(seq):
        ops[(t, pos)] = {"center": center, "proc": proc}
        total_proc_time += proc

# Big‑M value (larger than any possible makespan)
M = total_proc_time + 10   # safe upper bound

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Truck_Distribution_JobShop", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: start time of every operation
start = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "S",
    ops.keys(),
    lowBound=0,
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous,
)

# Makespan variable
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Precedence constraints (order inside each truck)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for t in routes.keys():
    for k in range(len(routes[t]) - 1):
        i = (t, k)
        j = (t, k + 1)
        model += (
            start[i] + ops[i]["proc"] <= start[j],
            f"Prec_T{t}_op{k}_to_op{k+1}",
        )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Disjunctive (machine) constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Group operations by centre
center_ops = {}
for op_key, attr in ops.items():
    c = attr["center"]
    center_ops.setdefault(c, []).append(op_key)

# Binary variables that decide the order of any two ops on the same centre
y = {}
for c, op_list in center_ops.items():
    for i_idx in range(len(op_list)):
        for j_idx in range(i_idx + 1, len(op_list)):
            i = op_list[i_idx]
            j = op_list[j_idx]
            var = pulp.LpVariable(
                f"Y_{i[0]}_{i[1]}_{j[0]}_{j[1]}", cat=pulp.LpBinary
            )
            y[(i, j)] = var

            # i before j  OR  j before i
            model += (
                start[i] + ops[i]["proc"]
                <= start[j] + M * (1 - var),
                f"Seq_{c}_{i[0]}_{i[1]}_before_{j[0]}_{j[1]}",
            )
            model += (
                start[j] + ops[j]["proc"]
                <= start[i] + M * var,
                f"Seq_{c}_{j[0]}_{j[1]}_before_{i[0]}_{i[1]}",
            )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Makespan definition
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for op_key, attr in ops.items():
    model += (
        Cmax >= start[op_key] + attr["proc"],
        f"Makespan_def_{op_key[0]}_{op_key[1]}",
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimize_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Optimal makespan (Cmax): {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times (truck, step) -> start")
for op_key in sorted(ops.keys()):
    print(f"Truck {op_key[0]}, step {op_key[1]+1}: {pulp.value(start[op_key]):.2f}")

"""
Job‑shop model for the 6‑truck, 6‑center problem.
Solves the makespan minimisation using PuLP + HiGHS.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Trucks are indexed 1..6, operations (stops) 0..5 (six stops per truck)

# processing times p[truck,op]
p = {
    (1, 0): 8, (1, 1): 8, (1, 2): 5, (1, 3): 1, (1, 4): 4, (1, 5): 9,
    (2, 0): 2, (2, 1): 5, (2, 2): 3, (2, 3):10, (2, 4): 7, (2, 5): 4,
    (3, 0): 6, (3, 1): 4, (3, 2): 6, (3, 3): 8, (3, 4): 4, (3, 5): 5,
    (4, 0): 3, (4, 1): 6, (4, 2): 1, (4, 3): 8, (4, 4): 1, (4, 5): 1,
    (5, 0): 1, (5, 1): 6, (5, 2): 7, (5, 3): 3, (5, 4): 4, (5, 5): 8,
    (6, 0): 7, (6, 1): 7, (6, 2): 1, (6, 3): 7, (6, 4): 5, (6, 5): 9,
}

# machines (distribution centres) m[truck,op]  (centres numbered 1..6)
m = {
    (1, 0): 5, (1, 1): 2, (1, 2): 4, (1, 3): 1, (1, 4): 3, (1, 5): 6,
    (2, 0): 6, (2, 1): 2, (2, 2): 4, (2, 3): 3, (2, 4): 5, (2, 5): 1,
    (3, 0): 3, (3, 1): 6, (3, 2): 4, (3, 3): 1, (3, 4): 5, (3, 5): 2,
    (4, 0): 3, (4, 1): 2, (4, 2): 6, (4, 3): 1, (4, 4): 5, (4, 5): 4,
    (5, 0): 2, (5, 1): 1, (5, 2): 5, (5, 3): 4, (5, 4): 6, (5, 5): 3,
    (6, 0): 4, (6, 1): 2, (6, 2): 3, (6, 3): 5, (6, 4): 1, (6, 5): 6,
}

TRUCKS = range(1, 7)          # 1..6
OPS    = range(0, 6)          # 0..5
M_BIG  = 200                  # big‑M (greater than total processing time)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Truck_Scheduling", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Start time variables S[t,o] >= 0   (continuous)
S = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("Start",
                          ((t, o) for t in TRUCKS for o in OPS),
                          lowBound=0,
                          cat='Continuous')

# Makespan variable
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Makespan", lowBound=0, cat='Continuous')

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimise_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Job (truck) precedence constraints
for t in TRUCKS:
    for o in OPS[:-1]:  # 0..4
        model += (S[(t, o+1)] >= S[(t, o)] + p[(t, o)],
                  f"Precedence_truck{t}_op{o}")

# 2) Machine (centre) capacity constraints – one‑at‑a‑time
#    For each pair of operations that share the same centre create a binary order variable.
order_vars = {}
for centre in range(1, 7):          # centres 1..6
    # collect all operations that use this centre
    ops_on_centre = [(t, o) for t in TRUCKS for o in OPS if m[(t, o)] == centre]
    # create ordering binaries for every unordered pair
    for i in range(len(ops_on_centre)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(ops_on_centre)):
            op1 = ops_on_centre[i]
            op2 = ops_on_centre[j]
            var_name = f"Y_{op1[0]}_{op1[1]}_{op2[0]}_{op2[1]}"
            y = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat='Binary')
            order_vars[(op1, op2)] = y

            # op1 before op2   (y = 1)  or op2 before op1 (y = 0)
            model += (S[op1] >= S[op2] + p[op2] - M_BIG * (1 - y),
                      f"Machine_{centre}_order1_{op1}_{op2}")
            model += (S[op2] >= S[op1] + p[op1] - M_BIG * y,
                      f"Machine_{centre}_order2_{op1}_{op2}")

# 3) Definition of makespan (must be at least the completion time of every truck)
for t in TRUCKS:
    last_op = (t, OPS[-1])                 # (t,5)
    model += (Cmax >= S[last_op] + p[last_op],
              f"Makespan_def_truck{t}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output (optional, can be removed if only the script is required)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Minimum makespan: {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times (truck, operation):")
for t in TRUCKS:
    for o in OPS:
        print(f"  Truck {t}, Op {o} (Centre {m[(t,o)]}): start = {pulp.value(S[(t,o)])}")

Solved with PuLP + HiGHS.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Trucks are indexed 1..6, operations (stops) 1..6.
# For each truck i and operation k we store the centre (machine) and the handling time.

# centre codes: C1..C6 -> integers 1..6
# (truck, operation): (machine, processing time)
data = {
    1: [(5, 8), (2, 8), (4, 5), (1, 1), (3, 4), (6, 9)],
    2: [(6, 2), (2, 5), (4, 3), (3,10), (5, 7), (1, 4)],
    3: [(3, 6), (6, 4), (4, 6), (1, 8), (5, 4), (2, 5)],
    4: [(3, 3), (2, 6), (6, 1), (1, 8), (5, 1), (4, 1)],
    5: [(2, 1), (1, 6), (5, 7), (4, 3), (6, 4), (3, 8)],
    6: [(4, 7), (2, 7), (3, 1), (5, 7), (1, 5), (6, 9)],
}

# Helper dictionaries for quick access
machine = {}   # machine[i,k] = centre number (1..6)
proc    = {}   # proc[i,k]    = handling time
for i in range(1, 7):
    for k, (c, t) in enumerate(data[i], start=1):
        machine[i, k] = c
        proc[i, k]    = t

# Upper bound for the big‑M (sum of all processing times + a safety margin)
M = sum(proc[i, k] for i in range(1, 7) for k in range(1, 7)) + 10   # 184 + 10 = 194

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Truck_Distribution_Centres_Scheduling", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Start time variables (continuous, >=0)
S = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("S", (range(1, 7), range(1, 7)), lowBound=0, cat='Continuous')

# Makespan variable
Z = pulp.LpVariable("Z", lowBound=0, cat='Continuous')

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise the makespan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Z, "Minimise_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Completion of the last operation of each truck must be <= Z
for i in range(1, 7):
    model += S[i, 6] + proc[i, 6] <= Z, f"makespan_truck_{i}"

# 2) Precedence constraints within each truck
for i in range(1, 7):
    for k in range(1, 6):          # operations 1..5 must finish before the next starts
        model += S[i, k+1] >= S[i, k] + proc[i, k], f"precedence_truck_{i}_op_{k}_to_{k+1}"

# 3) Disjunctive (machine capacity) constraints
# For each centre we generate all unordered pairs of operations that require it.
# A binary variable decides the order of the two operations.
y = {}   # y[(i,k,j,l)] = 1 if (i,k) is scheduled after (j,l)

for centre in range(1, 7):
    # collect all (i,k) that use this centre
    ops = [(i, k) for i in range(1, 7) for k in range(1, 7) if machine[i, k] == centre]

    # create constraints for every unordered pair
    for idx in range(len(ops)):
        i, k = ops[idx]
        for jdx in range(idx + 1, len(ops)):
            j, l = ops[jdx]

            # binary ordering variable (i,k) after (j,l) ?
            var_name = f"Y_{i}_{k}_{j}_{l}"
            y[(i, k, j, l)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat='Binary')

            # (i,k) starts after (j,l) finishes  if y = 1
            model += (
                S[i, k] >= S[j, l] + proc[j, l] - M * (1 - y[(i, k, j, l)]),
                f"machine_{centre}_order1_{i}_{k}_after_{j}_{l}"
            )
            # (j,l) starts after (i,k) finishes  if y = 0
            model += (
                S[j, l] >= S[i, k] + proc[i, k] - M * y[(i, k, j, l)],
                f"machine_{centre}_order2_{j}_{l}_after_{i}_{k}"
            )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Status: {status}")

if status == "Optimal" or status == "Feasible":
    print(f"Minimum makespan (total completion time): {pulp.value(Z)}\n")
    for i in range(1, 7):
        print(f"Truck {i} schedule:")
        for k in range(1, 7):
            start = pulp.value(S[i, k])
            finish = start + proc[i, k]
            centre = machine[i, k]
            print(f"  Op {k}: Centre C{centre}, start {start:.2f}, finish {finish:.2f}, time {proc[i, k]}")
        print()
else:
    print("No feasible solution found.")

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Job‑shop model for the 6‑truck, 6‑center logistics problem.
All data are taken directly from the statement.
The model is solved with PuLP + HiGHS.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Trucks are indexed 1..6, operations (stops) are indexed 1..6 in the given order.
# Each entry: (center, handling_time)
routes = {
    1: [(5, 8), (2, 8), (4, 5), (1, 1), (3, 4), (6, 9)],
    2: [(6, 2), (2, 5), (4, 3), (3,10), (5, 7), (1, 4)],
    3: [(3, 6), (6, 4), (4, 6), (1, 8), (5, 4), (2, 5)],
    4: [(3, 3), (2, 6), (6, 1), (1, 8), (5, 1), (4, 1)],
    5: [(2, 1), (1, 6), (5, 7), (4, 3), (6, 4), (3, 8)],
    6: [(4, 7), (2, 7), (3, 1), (5, 7), (1, 5), (6, 9)]
}

# Upper bound for the big‑M (worst possible makespan)
M = 200.0

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Logistics_JobShop", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: start time of each operation (truck, operation index)
start = {}
proc_time = {}          # processing time for quick lookup
center_of = {}          # centre of each operation
for t in range(1, 7):
    for k, (c, p) in enumerate(routes[t], start=1):
        var_name = f"S_{t}_{k}"
        start[(t, k)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")
        proc_time[(t, k)] = p
        center_of[(t, k)] = c

# Makespan variable
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise makespan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimise_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Job (truck) precedence constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for t in range(1, 7):
    for k in range(1, 6):          # 5 precedence arcs per truck
        model += (start[(t, k + 1)] >=
                  start[(t, k)] + proc_time[(t, k)]), f"Prec_truck_{t}_op_{k}_to_{k+1}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Machine (center) capacity constraints – one‑at‑a‑time
#    Using binary ordering variables y_{i,j}
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Collect operations per centre
ops_per_center = {c: [] for c in range(1, 7)}
for (t, k), c in center_of.items():
    ops_per_center[c].append((t, k))

# Binary variables: y[(i),(j)] == 1 if operation i finishes before j starts
y = {}
for c in range(1, 7):
    ops = ops_per_center[c]
    # create binary for each unordered pair
    for idx1 in range(len(ops)):
        for idx2 in range(idx1 + 1, len(ops)):
            i = ops[idx1]
            j = ops[idx2]
            var_name = f"Y_{i[0]}_{i[1]}_before_{j[0]}_{j[1]}"
            y[(i, j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")
            # i before j
            model += (start[j] >= start[i] + proc_time[i] - M * (1 - y[(i, j)]),
                      f"Machine_{c}_order_{i}_before_{j}")
            # j before i
            model += (start[i] >= start[j] + proc_time[j] - M * y[(i, j)],
                      f"Machine_{c}_order_{j}_before_{i}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Makespan definition
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for t in range(1, 7):
    for k in range(1, 7):
        model += (Cmax >= start[(t, k)] + proc_time[(t, k)]), f"Makespan_def_{t}_{k}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

    # T6
    [(4, 7), (2, 7), (3, 1), (5, 7), (1, 5), (6, 9)],
]

ops_per_truck = len(routes[0])    # 6

# Separate the data for easier access
center = {}   # center[t,k] = machine (1..6)
proc   = {}   # proc[t,k]   = processing time
for t in range(num_trucks):
    for k in range(ops_per_truck):
        c, p = routes[t][k]
        center[t, k] = c
        proc[t, k]   = p

# Big‑M value (larger than any possible makespan)
M = sum(proc[t, k] for t in range(num_trucks) for k in range(ops_per_truck)) + 10  # 194

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Logistics_JobShop", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: start time of each operation (continuous, >=0)
S = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "Start",
    ((t, k) for t in range(num_trucks) for k in range(ops_per_truck)),
    lowBound=0,
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous,
)

# Makespan variable
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# Binary variables for the disjunctive (ordering) constraints on each centre
Y = {}   # Y[(t1,k1,t2,k2)] = 1  => operation (t1,k1) precedes (t2,k2) on the same centre
for t1 in range(num_trucks):
    for k1 in range(ops_per_truck):

for t in range(num_trucks):
    for k in range(ops_per_truck):

            S[t, k + 1] >= S[t, k] + proc[t, k],

jobs = {

           ("DC5", 10), ("DC10", 9), ("DC3", 2), ("DC6", 1), ("DC2", 2)],

    "T9": [("DC6", 8), ("DC4", 10), ("DC3", 3), ("DC1", 7), ("DC8", 1),
           ("DC9", 9), ("DC7", 1), ("DC2", 9), ("DC5", 4), ("DC10", 9)],
    "T10": [("DC10", 6), ("DC6", 4), ("DC1", 2), ("DC7", 7), ("DC2", 4),
            ("DC8", 3), ("DC5", 4), ("DC4", 8), ("DC3", 10), ("DC9", 7)]
}

machines = ["DC1","DC2","DC3","DC4","DC5","DC6","DC7","DC8","DC9","DC10"]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Truck_Distribution_Center_Scheduling", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: start time of each operation (continuous, >=0)
start = {}
proc_time = {}   # processing time lookup
machine_of = {}  # machine of each operation

    for idx, (mach, pt) in enumerate(ops):
        key = (job, idx)                     # unique identifier

#    Big‑M is the sum of all processing times (a safe upper bound).

    for i in range(len(op_list)):

            op_j = op_list[j]

    last_key = (job, last_idx)
    model += (Cmax >= start[last_key] + proc_time[last_key],
              f"Makespan_def_{job}")

# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

        model += s[(j, k)] + p_ik <= s[(j, k + 1)], f"Job_{j}_op_{k}_to_{k+1}"

# 2) Machine capacity – no overlap on the same DC
#    Use binary variables y_{i,j} for each unordered pair of operations on the same machine.
y = {}   # key = (m, j1, k1, j2, k2) with (j1,k1) < (j2,k2) in lexical order
for m in range(num_machines):
    ops = machine_to_ops[m]          # list of (job, op_index)
    # iterate over unordered pairs
    for idx1 in range(len(ops)):
        j1, k1 = ops[idx1]
        p1 = jobs_data[j1][k1][1]
        for idx2 in range(idx1 + 1, len(ops)):
            j2, k2 = ops[idx2]
            p2 = jobs_data[j2][k2][1]

            # binary variable: 1 if (j1,k1) precedes (j2,k2)
            y_var = pulp.LpVariable(f"y_m{m}_j{j1}k{k1}_j{j2}k{k2}", cat="Binary")
            y[(m, j1, k1, j2, k2)] = y_var

            # (j1,k1) before (j2,k2)
            model += (
                s[(j1, k1)] + p1
                <= s[(j2, k2)] + big_M * (1 - y_var),
                f"Machine_{m}_pair_{j1}_{k1}_before_{j2}_{k2}",
            )
            # (j2,k2) before (j1,k1)
            model += (
                s[(j2, k2)] + p2
                <= s[(j1, k1)] + big_M * y_var,
                f"Machine_{m}_pair_{j2}_{k2}_before_{j1}_{k1}",
            )

# 3) Definition of makespan
for j in range(num_jobs):
    last_k = ops_per_job - 1
    p_last = jobs_data[j][last_k][1]
    model += s[(j, last_k)] + p_last <= Cmax, f"Makespan_job_{j}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print("Status :", pulp.LpStatus[model.status])
print("Minimum makespan (total completion time) :", pulp.value(Cmax))

# Optional: print start times for each truck
for j in range(num_jobs):
    print(f"\nTruck T{j+1} schedule:")
    for k in range(ops_per_job):
        m, p = jobs_data[j][k]
        start = pulp.value(s[(j, k)])
        print(f"  Op {k+1}: DC{m+1} (proc {p})  -> start {start:.2f}, finish {start + p:.2f}")

}

# Helper structures
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# (truck, operation_index) -> machine, processing time
ops = {}
for t, seq in trucks.items():
    for k, (machine, proc) in enumerate(seq, start=1):
        ops[(t, k)] = {"machine": machine, "proc": proc}

# List of all operations
all_ops = list(ops.keys())

# Operations grouped by machine (distribution centre)
machine_ops = {}
for (t, k), info in ops.items():
    m = info["machine"]
    machine_ops.setdefault(m, []).append((t, k))

# Upper bound M for big‑M constraints (sum of all processing times is safe)
M = sum(info["proc"] for info in ops.values())

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Logistics_JobShop", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: start time of each operation
S = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("Start",
                          all_ops,
                          lowBound=0,
                          cat="Continuous")

# Makespan variable
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise makespan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimise_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for t, seq in trucks.items():
    for k in range(1, len(seq)):
        # operation k must finish before operation k+1 starts
        model += (S[(t, k + 1)] >= S[(t, k)] + ops[(t, k)]["proc"],
                  f"Prec_truck{t}_op{k}_to_{k+1}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Disjunctive (machine capacity) constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Y = {}  # binary ordering variables for pairs sharing a machine
for m, oplist in machine_ops.items():
    # create a binary variable for each unordered pair (i,j) on the same machine
    for i in range(len(oplist)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(oplist)):
            op_i = oplist[i]
            op_j = oplist[j]
            var_name = f"Y_{op_i[0]}_{op_i[1]}_{op_j[0]}_{op_j[1]}"
            Y[(op_i, op_j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")

            pi = ops[op_i]["proc"]
            pj = ops[op_j]["proc"]

            # i before j  (Y = 1)  OR  j before i (Y = 0)
            model += (S[op_j] >= S[op_i] + pi - M * (1 - Y[(op_i, op_j)]),
                      f"Mach{m}_order_{op_i}_before_{op_j}")
            model += (S[op_i] >= S[op_j] + pj - M * Y[(op_i, op_j)],
                      f"Mach{m}_order_{op_j}_before_{op_i}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Definition of makespan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for (t, k), info in ops.items():
    model += (Cmax >= S[(t, k)] + info["proc"], f"Cmax_def_truck{t}_op{k}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve with HiGHS (time limit 120 seconds)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output results
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Minimum makespan (Cmax): {pulp.value(Cmax):.2f}\n")

# Create a sorted list of operations by start time for readability
schedule = []
for (t, k), var in S.items():
    schedule.append((pulp.value(var), t, k,
                     ops[(t, k)]["machine"],
                     ops[(t, k)]["proc"]))
schedule.sort()

print("Schedule (Start, Truck, Op#, Machine, ProcessingTime):")
for start, t, k, m, p in schedule:
    print(f"{start:6.2f}  Truck{t:2d}  Op{k:2d}  DC{m:2d}  proc={p}")

# End of script

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Job‑shop model for the 10‑truck / 10‑distribution‑center problem.
Each truck (job) has a fixed sequence of operations (center, handling time).
The goal is to minimise the makespan (completion time of the last truck).

The model is built with PuLP and solved by HiGHS.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Data definition
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Trucks are numbered 1..10, distribution centres are DC1..DC10.
# For each truck we list the ordered pairs (centre, handling time).

routes = {
    1: [("DC2", 7), ("DC5", 7), ("DC8", 10), ("DC7", 9), ("DC3", 5),
        ("DC10", 10), ("DC4", 8), ("DC9", 7), ("DC6", 4), ("DC1", 3)],
    2: [("DC8", 2), ("DC5", 6), ("DC3", 2), ("DC1", 1), ("DC9", 4),
        ("DC2", 2), ("DC6", 10), ("DC4", 6), ("DC10", 9), ("DC7", 1)],
    3: [("DC5", 1), ("DC8", 1), ("DC7", 1), ("DC1", 4), ("DC2", 2),
        ("DC3", 1), ("DC6", 8), ("DC9", 2), ("DC4", 5), ("DC10", 4)],
    4: [("DC9", 1), ("DC6", 9), ("DC7", 10), ("DC2", 10), ("DC8", 7),
        ("DC5", 10), ("DC10", 8), ("DC4", 3), ("DC3", 7), ("DC1", 10)],
    5: [("DC9", 6), ("DC10", 10), ("DC2", 7), ("DC8", 7), ("DC5", 5),
        ("DC7", 4), ("DC3", 7), ("DC4", 7), ("DC1", 10), ("DC6", 7)],
    6: [("DC9", 6), ("DC4", 6), ("DC8", 8), ("DC1", 10), ("DC7", 5),
        ("DC5", 10), ("DC10", 9), ("DC3", 2), ("DC6", 1), ("DC2", 2)],
    7: [("DC5", 5), ("DC3", 7), ("DC10", 5), ("DC6", 2), ("DC2", 9),
        ("DC1", 10), ("DC8", 1), ("DC9", 1), ("DC4", 3), ("DC7", 4)],
    8: [("DC2", 8), ("DC7", 10), ("DC3", 2), ("DC6", 9), ("DC5", 4),
        ("DC9", 9), ("DC8", 8), ("DC1", 3), ("DC4", 8), ("DC10", 10)],
    9: [("DC6", 8), ("DC4", 10), ("DC3", 3), ("DC1", 7), ("DC8", 1),
        ("DC9", 9), ("DC7", 1), ("DC2", 9), ("DC5", 4), ("DC10", 9)],
    10:[("DC10", 6), ("DC6", 4), ("DC1", 2), ("DC7", 7), ("DC2", 4),
        ("DC8", 3), ("DC5", 4), ("DC4", 8), ("DC3", 10), ("DC9", 7)]
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Build a list of all operations with unique identifiers
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
operations = []          # list of dicts, each dict describes one operation
total_processing = 0

for truck_id, seq in routes.items():
    for op_idx, (center, proc) in enumerate(seq, start=1):
        name = f"T{truck_id}_O{op_idx}"
        operations.append({
            "job": truck_id,
            "op_index": op_idx,
            "machine": center,
            "proc": proc,
            "name": name
        })
        total_processing += proc

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Model definition
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Truck_Distribution_Scheduling", pulp.LpMinimize)

# 3.1 Decision variables: start time of each operation (continuous, >=0)
S = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("Start",
                          [op["name"] for op in operations],
                          lowBound=0,
                          cat="Continuous")

# 3.2 Makespan variable
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Objective: minimise makespan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimise_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5.1 Job‑precedence constraints (operations of the same truck)
for truck_id, seq in routes.items():
    for k in range(len(seq) - 1):
        cur_name = f"T{truck_id}_O{k+1}"
        nxt_name = f"T{truck_id}_O{k+2}"
        cur_proc = seq[k][1]
        model += (S[nxt_name] >= S[cur_name] + cur_proc,
                  f"Precedence_T{truck_id}_O{k+1}_to_O{k+2}")

# 5.2 Disjunctive (machine capacity) constraints
# For each pair of operations that need the same centre we introduce a binary
# variable that decides their order.
# Big‑M is set to the sum of all processing times (an absolute upper bound).
M = total_processing + 1   # a safe big‑M

# Helper: collect operations per machine
from collections import defaultdict
ops_per_machine = defaultdict(list)
for op in operations:
    ops_per_machine[op["machine"]].append(op)

Y = {}   # binary ordering variables

for machine, ops in ops_per_machine.items():
    # create ordering variable for every unordered pair
    for i in range(len(ops)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(ops)):
            op_i = ops[i]
            op_j = ops[j]
            name_i = op_i["name"]
            name_j = op_j["name"]
            var_name = f"Y_{name_i}_{name_j}"
            Y[(name_i, name_j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")
            # If Y=1 then i before j, else j before i
            # i before j
            model += (S[name_j] >= S[name_i] + op_i["proc"] - M * (1 - Y[(name_i, name_j)]),
                      f"Machine_{machine}_{name_i}_before_{name_j}")
            # j before i
            model += (S[name_i] >= S[name_j] + op_j["proc"] - M * Y[(name_i, name_j)],
                      f"Machine_{machine}_{name_j}_before_{name_i}")

# 5.3 Makespan must be at least the completion time of each truck's last operation
for truck_id, seq in routes.items():
    last_op_name = f"T{truck_id}_O{len(seq)}"
    last_proc = seq[-1][1]
    model += (Cmax >= S[last_op_name] + last_proc,
              f"Makespan_ge_last_T{truck_id}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Solve with HiGHS
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Output results
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Minimum makespan (Cmax): {pulp.value(Cmax):.2f}\n")

print("Start times (in the same unit as handling times):")
for op in sorted(operations, key=lambda o: (o["job"], o["op_index"])):
    start_val = pulp.value(S[op["name"]])
    print(f"{op['name']:12s} (Truck {op['job']}, Centre {op['machine']}) : {start_val:.2f}")

# Optional: display ordering decisions for one centre as a sanity check
# (comment out if not needed)
# for machine, ops in ops_per_machine.items():
#     if len(ops) > 1:
#         print(f"\nOrdering on {machine}:")
#         for i in range(len(ops)):

#                 y_val = pulp.value(Y[key])

#                     order = f"{ops[i]['name']} before {ops[j]['name']}" if y_val > 0.5 else f"{ops[j]['name']} before {ops[i]['name']}"

"""
Job‑shop scheduling model for three patients and three devices.
Each test (operation) must be performed without interruption,
each device can handle only one test at a time.
The model minimizes the makespan (completion time of the last test).
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Operations are identified by a tuple (patient, index)
# patient: "A", "B", "C"
# index: 1,2,3 (order in the patient's plan)

operations = {
    ("A", 1): {"machine": "X", "proc": 2},
    ("A", 2): {"machine": "Z", "proc": 4},
    ("A", 3): {"machine": "Y", "proc": 6},
    ("B", 1): {"machine": "X", "proc": 1},
    ("B", 2): {"machine": "Y", "proc": 2},
    ("B", 3): {"machine": "Z", "proc": 3},
    ("C", 1): {"machine": "Z", "proc": 10},
    ("C", 2): {"machine": "X", "proc": 9},
    ("C", 3): {"machine": "Y", "proc": 10},
}

# Big‑M value (larger than any possible makespan)
M = 100

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Hospital_Test_Scheduling", pulp.LpMinimize)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Decision variables
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Start time of each operation (continuous, >=0)
start = {
    op: pulp.LpVariable(f"start_{op[0]}{op[1]}", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")
    for op in operations
}

# Makespan (continuous, >=0)
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Binary ordering variables for every unordered pair of operations that share a machine
order = {}
for m in ["X", "Y", "Z"]:
    # collect operations on this machine
    ops_on_m = [op for op, data in operations.items() if data["machine"] == m]
    # create binary variable for each unordered pair
    for i in range(len(ops_on_m)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(ops_on_m)):
            op_i = ops_on_m[i]
            op_j = ops_on_m[j]
            var = pulp.LpVariable(f"y_{op_i[0]}{op_i[1]}_before_{op_j[0]}{op_j[1]}", cat="Binary")
            order[(op_i, op_j)] = var

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise makespan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimise_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Makespan must be at least the completion time of every operation
for op, data in operations.items():
    model += Cmax >= start[op] + data["proc"], f"Makespan_ge_{op[0]}{op[1]}"

# 2) Precedence constraints inside each patient (strict sequence)
patient_sequences = {
    "A": [("A", 1), ("A", 2), ("A", 3)],
    "B": [("B", 1), ("B", 2), ("B", 3)],
    "C": [("C", 1), ("C", 2), ("C", 3)],
}
for pat, seq in patient_sequences.items():
    for k in range(len(seq) - 1):
        op_cur = seq[k]
        op_next = seq[k + 1]
        model += (
            start[op_cur] + operations[op_cur]["proc"] <= start[op_next],
            f"Precedence_{op_cur[0]}{op_cur[1]}_to_{op_next[0]}{op_next[1]}",
        )

# 3) Disjunctive (no‑overlap) constraints on each machine using binary ordering variables
for (op_i, op_j), y_ij in order.items():
    p_i = operations[op_i]["proc"]
    p_j = operations[op_j]["proc"]
    # either i precedes j
    model += start[op_i] + p_i <= start[op_j] + M * (1 - y_ij), f"Seq_{op_i}_before_{op_j}"
    # or j precedes i
    model += start[op_j] + p_j <= start[op_i] + M * y_ij, f"Seq_{op_j}_before_{op_i}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print("Status:", pulp.LpStatus[model.status])
print(f"Minimum makespan (total time) = {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")
print("Start times:")
for op in sorted(operations):
    st = pulp.value(start[op])
    print(f" Patient {op[0]}, Test {op[1]} (Machine {operations[op]['machine']}, "
          f"Duration {operations[op]['proc']}): start at {st}")

# optional: show ordering decisions (useful for verification)
print("\nMachine ordering decisions (y = 1 means first operation precedes second):")
for (op_i, op_j), y_ij in order.items():
    print(f" {op_i[0]}{op_i[1]} before {op_j[0]}{op_j[1]} : {pulp.value(y_ij)}")

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
# Job‑shop scheduling model for three patients (jobs) and three devices (machines)
# Solved with PuLP and the HiGHS solver

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Jobs (patients) and their ordered operations: (machine, processing time)
jobs = {
    "A": [("X", 2), ("Z", 4), ("Y", 6)],
    "B": [("X", 1), ("Y", 2), ("Z", 3)],
    "C": [("Z",10), ("X", 9), ("Y",10)]
}

# Create a list of all operations with a unique identifier
# op_id is a tuple (job, index) where index starts at 0
ops = []
proc_time = {}          # processing time of each operation
machine_of = {}         # machine required by each operation
for job, seq in jobs.items():
    for idx, (mach, dur) in enumerate(seq):
        op = (job, idx)
        ops.append(op)
        proc_time[op] = dur
        machine_of[op] = mach

# Big‑M value (larger than any feasible makespan)
M = sum(proc_time.values())   # 47 in this instance, safe upper bound

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Hospital_Test_Scheduling", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: start time of each operation (continuous, >=0)
start = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("S", ops, lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Makespan variable
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Binary variables for ordering of any two operations that share a machine
# For each unordered pair (i,j) with i<j on the same machine we create y_ij
y = {}
for i in range(len(ops)):
    for j in range(i+1, len(ops)):
        op_i = ops[i]
        op_j = ops[j]
        if machine_of[op_i] == machine_of[op_j]:          # same equipment
            y[(op_i, op_j)] = pulp.LpVariable(f"Y_{op_i}_{op_j}", cat="Binary")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise makespan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimise_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Job precedence (operations must follow the given order)
for job, seq in jobs.items():
    for idx in range(len(seq)-1):
        op_cur = (job, idx)
        op_next = (job, idx+1)
        model += (start[op_next] >= start[op_cur] + proc_time[op_cur],
                  f"Precedence_{op_cur}_to_{op_next}")

# 2) Disjunctive constraints for operations that share a machine
for (op_i, op_j), y_var in y.items():
    # op_i before op_j  (or the opposite) – encoded with binary y_var
    model += (start[op_i] + proc_time[op_i] <= start[op_j] + M * (1 - y_var),
              f"Seq_{op_i}_before_{op_j}")
    model += (start[op_j] + proc_time[op_j] <= start[op_i] + M * y_var,
              f"Seq_{op_j}_before_{op_i}")

# 3) Definition of makespan – it must be at least the completion time of each job
for job, seq in jobs.items():
    last_op = (job, len(seq)-1)
    model += (Cmax >= start[last_op] + proc_time[last_op],
              f"Makespan_{job}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Status: {status}")
print(f"Minimum makespan (total time): {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times for each operation (patient, operation index):")
for op in ops:
    print(f"  {op}: start = {pulp.value(start[op]):.2f}, "
          f"machine = {machine_of[op]}, duration = {proc_time[op]}")

"""
Job‑shop scheduling model for three patients (jobs) and three devices (machines).

Objective: minimise the makespan (completion time of the last test).
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# (patient, operation_index, machine, processing_time)
operations = [
    # Patient A
    ("A", 1, "X", 2),
    ("A", 2, "Z", 4),
    ("A", 3, "Y", 6),
    # Patient B
    ("B", 1, "X", 1),
    ("B", 2, "Y", 2),
    ("B", 3, "Z", 3),
    # Patient C
    ("C", 1, "Z", 10),
    ("C", 2, "X", 9),
    ("C", 3, "Y", 10),
]

# Helper structures
# key: (patient, op_index) -> (machine, proc_time)
proc = {(p, o): (m, t) for (p, o, m, t) in operations}

# List of patients (jobs) in order of operations
jobs = {
    "A": [1, 2, 3],
    "B": [1, 2, 3],
    "C": [1, 2, 3],
}

# Machines
machines = ["X", "Y", "Z"]

# Big‑M value (larger than any possible makespan)
M = sum(t for (_, _, _, t) in operations)  # 47 in this instance

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Hospital_Test_Scheduling", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: start time of each operation (continuous, >=0)
start = {}
for (p, o, m, t) in operations:
    var_name = f"start_{p}_{o}"
    start[(p, o)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Makespan variable
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("makespan", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Binary variables for ordering of any two operations that need the same machine
order = {}   # key: ((p1,o1),(p2,o2)) with p1,o1 < p2,o2 lexicographically
for m in machines:
    # collect all operations that require machine m
    ops_on_m = [(p, o) for (p, o, mach, _) in operations if mach == m]
    # create binary variable for each unordered pair
    for i in range(len(ops_on_m)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(ops_on_m)):
            a = ops_on_m[i]
            b = ops_on_m[j]
            var_name = f"order_{a[0]}{a[1]}_before_{b[0]}{b[1]}"
            order[(a, b)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimise_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Completion time definition for makespan
for (p, o, m, t) in operations:
    model += Cmax >= start[(p, o)] + t, f"makespan_def_{p}_{o}"

# 2. Precedence constraints within each patient (job)
for p, ops in jobs.items():
    for k in range(len(ops) - 1):
        o_cur = ops[k]
        o_next = ops[k + 1]
        t_cur = proc[(p, o_cur)][1]
        model += (
            start[(p, o_next)] >= start[(p, o_cur)] + t_cur,
            f"precedence_{p}_{o_cur}_to_{o_next}",
        )

# 3. Disjunctive (machine capacity) constraints
for ((p1, o1), (p2, o2)), y in order.items():
    m1, t1 = proc[(p1, o1)]
    m2, t2 = proc[(p2, o2)]
    # both operations use the same machine by construction
    # a) if y = 1 then operation (p1,o1) precedes (p2,o2)
    model += (
        start[(p2, o2)] >= start[(p1, o1)] + t1 - M * (1 - y),
        f"machine_{m1}_seq1_{p1}{o1}_before_{p2}{o2}",
    )
    # b) if y = 0 then operation (p2,o2) precedes (p1,o1)
    model += (
        start[(p1, o1)] >= start[(p2, o2)] + t2 - M * y,
        f"machine_{m1}_seq2_{p2}{o2}_before_{p1}{o1}",
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Minimum makespan: {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times (in same time units as durations):")
for (p, o) in sorted(start.keys()):
    print(f"  Patient {p} operation {o} (Machine {proc[(p,o)][0]}, duration {proc[(p,o)][1]}): "
          f"start = {pulp.value(start[(p,o)])}")

# Optional: show the order decisions (useful for debugging)
# for ((p1,o1),(p2,o2)), y in order.items():
#     if pulp.value(y) > 0.5:

# Job‑shop scheduling for three patients (jobs) and three devices (machines)
# using PuLP and the HiGHS solver.

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Jobs (patients) and their ordered operations: (machine, processing time)
jobs = {
    "A": [("X", 2), ("Z", 4), ("Y", 6)],
    "B": [("X", 1), ("Y", 2), ("Z", 3)],
    "C": [("Z", 10), ("X", 9), ("Y", 10)],
}

# Create a flat list of operations with unique IDs
ops = []                     # list of operation identifiers
proc_time = {}               # processing time of each operation
machine_of = {}              # machine required by each operation
job_of = {}                  # job to which each operation belongs
op_index = {}                # (job, position) -> op id

op_id = 0
for job, seq in jobs.items():
    for pos, (mach, dur) in enumerate(seq, start=1):
        oid = f"{job}{pos}"               # e.g., "A1", "B2", …
        ops.append(oid)
        proc_time[oid] = dur
        machine_of[oid] = mach
        job_of[oid] = job
        op_index[(job, pos)] = oid
        op_id += 1

# Machines and the operations that need them
machines = {}
for oid in ops:
    mach = machine_of[oid]
    machines.setdefault(mach, []).append(oid)

# Big‑M (larger than any possible makespan)
M = sum(proc_time.values()) + 10   # 47 + 10 = 57, safe upper bound

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Hospital_Test_Scheduling", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
#   start[oid]  – continuous start time of operation oid
start = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("Start", ops, lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

#   Cmax – makespan (completion time of the last operation)
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

#   y[(i,j)] – binary ordering variable for each pair of ops sharing a machine
y = {}
for mach, op_list in machines.items():
    n = len(op_list)
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            o_i = op_list[i]
            o_j = op_list[j]
            var = pulp.LpVariable(f"y_{o_i}_{o_j}", cat="Binary")
            y[(o_i, o_j)] = var
            # (o_i before o_j)  =>  y = 1
            # (o_j before o_i)  =>  y = 0

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimize_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Job precedence constraints (operations must follow the given order)
for job, seq in jobs.items():
    for pos in range(1, len(seq)):
        prev = op_index[(job, pos)]
        nxt = op_index[(job, pos + 1)]
        model += (
            start[nxt] >= start[prev] + proc_time[prev],
            f"Precedence_{prev}_before_{nxt}",
        )

# 2) Machine capacity (disjunctive) constraints using binary ordering vars
for (o_i, o_j), y_ij in y.items():
    # o_i before o_j
    model += (
        start[o_j] >= start[o_i] + proc_time[o_i] - M * (1 - y_ij),
        f"Machine_{machine_of[o_i]}_{o_i}_before_{o_j}",
    )
    # o_j before o_i
    model += (
        start[o_i] >= start[o_j] + proc_time[o_j] - M * y_ij,
        f"Machine_{machine_of[o_i]}_{o_j}_before_{o_i}",
    )

# 3) Makespan definition
for oid in ops:
    model += (
        Cmax >= start[oid] + proc_time[oid],
        f"Makespan_def_{oid}",
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Minimum makespan (total time): {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times:")
for oid in sorted(ops):
    print(f"  Operation {oid} (Job {job_of[oid]}, Machine {machine_of[oid]}, "
          f"Duration {proc_time[oid]}): start at {pulp.value(start[oid]):.2f}")

print("\nOperation order on each machine:")
for mach, op_list in machines.items():
    # sort operations by their start times
    ordered = sorted(op_list, key=lambda o: pulp.value(start[o]))
    order_str = " -> ".join(f"{o}({pulp.value(start[o]):.1f})" for o in ordered)
    print(f"  {mach}: {order_str}")

"""
Job‑shop model for the three‑patient, three‑device scheduling problem.
Solves the makespan minimisation with PuLP + HiGHS.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Patients (jobs) and their ordered operations (machine, duration)
jobs = {
    "A": [("X", 2), ("Z", 4), ("Y", 6)],
    "B": [("X", 1), ("Y", 2), ("Z", 3)],
    "C": [("Z",10), ("X", 9), ("Y",10)]
}

# Create a flat list of operations with a unique ID
ops = []                     # list of (op_id, job, index, machine, dur)
for job, seq in jobs.items():
    for idx, (mach, dur) in enumerate(seq):
        op_id = f"{job}{idx+1}"               # e.g. A1, B2 …
        ops.append((op_id, job, idx, mach, dur))

# Mapping for quick access
machine_of = {op_id: mach for op_id, _, _, mach, _ in ops}
duration_of = {op_id: dur for op_id, _, _, _, dur in ops}
job_of = {op_id: job for op_id, job, _, _, _ in ops}
index_in_job = {op_id: idx for op_id, _, idx, _, _ in ops}

# Set of machines
machines = set(machine_of.values())

# Big‑M (larger than any feasible makespan)
M = 100

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Hospital_Test_Scheduling", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Continuous start‑time variables for every operation
start = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("Start", [op_id for op_id, *_ in ops],
                              lowBound=0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# Makespan variable
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Makespan", lowBound=0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# Binary ordering variables for each unordered pair that shares a machine
# y[i,j] = 1  ⇒  operation i finishes before j starts
y = {}
for i in range(len(ops)):
    for j in range(i+1, len(ops)):
        op_i = ops[i][0]
        op_j = ops[j][0]
        if machine_of[op_i] == machine_of[op_j]:   # same equipment
            var_name = f"y_{op_i}_{op_j}"
            y[(op_i, op_j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat=pulp.LpBinary)

# --------------------
# Objective: minimise makespan
# --------------------
model += Cmax

# --------------------
# 1) Job‑precedence constraints (patient order)
# --------------------
for op_id, job, idx, mach, dur in ops:
    # look for the next operation of the same patient
    if idx + 1 < len(jobs[job]):          # there is a successor
        succ_id = f"{job}{idx+2}"
        model += start[succ_id] >= start[op_id] + duration_of[op_id]

# --------------------
# 2) Machine capacity (disjunctive) constraints
# --------------------
for (i, j), y_ij in y.items():
    # i before j
    model += start[i] + duration_of[i] <= start[j] + M * (1 - y_ij)
    # j before i
    model += start[j] + duration_of[j] <= start[i] + M * y_ij

# --------------------
# 3) Makespan definition
# --------------------
for op_id, _, _, _, _ in ops:
    model += Cmax >= start[op_id] + duration_of[op_id]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve with HiGHS (no console output, 2‑minute time limit)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output results
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Optimal makespan: {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times (in same time units as durations):")
for op_id, _, _, _, _ in sorted(ops, key=lambda x: (job_of[x[0]], index_in_job[x[0]])):
    print(f"  {op_id} (Patient {job_of[op_id]}, Machine {machine_of[op_id]}): "
          f"{pulp.value(start[op_id]):.2f}")

# Optional: show ordering decisions on each machine
print("\nMachine ordering (y = 1 means first op finishes before second):")
for (i, j), y_ij in y.items():
    if pulp.value(y_ij) > 0.5:
        order = f"{i} → {j}"
    else:
        order = f"{j} → {i}"
    print(f"  Machine {machine_of[i]}: {order}")

# Hospital job‑shop scheduling – minimize makespan
# Three patients, three tests each, each test needs a specific device.
# Solved with PuLP and the HiGHS solver.

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Operations are identified by an integer 1..9.
# For each operation we store: (patient, order_in_patient, device, duration)
ops_data = {
    1: ("A", 1, "X", 2),   # Patient A – operation 1
    2: ("A", 2, "Z", 4),   # Patient A – operation 2
    3: ("A", 3, "Y", 6),   # Patient A – operation 3
    4: ("B", 1, "X", 1),   # Patient B – operation 1
    5: ("B", 2, "Y", 2),   # Patient B – operation 2
    6: ("B", 3, "Z", 3),   # Patient B – operation 3
    7: ("C", 1, "Z", 10),  # Patient C – operation 1
    8: ("C", 2, "X", 9),   # Patient C – operation 2
    9: ("C", 3, "Y", 10)   # Patient C – operation 3
}

# Group operations by device (machine) – needed for disjunctive constraints
device_to_ops = {"X": [], "Y": [], "Z": []}
for i, (_, _, dev, _) in ops_data.items():
    device_to_ops[dev].append(i)

# Big‑M value – larger than any possible makespan
M = sum(dur for (_, _, _, dur) in ops_data.values()) + 10   # 47 + 10 = 57

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Hospital_JobShop", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables:
#   start_i : start time of operation i (continuous, >=0)
#   Cmax    : makespan (continuous, >=0)
#   y_i_j   : binary variable, 1 if operation i precedes j on the same device
start = {i: pulp.LpVariable(f"start_{i}", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")
         for i in ops_data}
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Binary ordering variables for every unordered pair of operations that share a device
y = {}
for dev, op_list in device_to_ops.items():
    for i_idx in range(len(op_list)):
        for j_idx in range(i_idx + 1, len(op_list)):
            i = op_list[i_idx]
            j = op_list[j_idx]
            y[(i, j)] = pulp.LpVariable(f"y_{i}_{j}", cat="Binary")   # 1 ⇒ i before j

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Objective: minimise makespan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimise_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4.1. Each operation must finish before the makespan
for i, (_, _, _, dur) in ops_data.items():
    model += start[i] + dur <= Cmax, f"makespan_after_op_{i}"

# 4.2. Precedence constraints inside each patient (given order must be respected)
#   A: 1→2→3, B: 4→5→6, C: 7→8→9
patient_sequences = {
    "A": [1, 2, 3],
    "B": [4, 5, 6],
    "C": [7, 8, 9]
}
for pat, seq in patient_sequences.items():
    for first, second in zip(seq, seq[1:]):
        dur_first = ops_data[first][3]
        model += start[second] >= start[first] + dur_first, f"patient_{pat}_order_{first}_before_{second}"

# 4.3. Disjunctive (machine) constraints – only one operation at a time on each device
for (i, j), y_ij in y.items():
    dur_i = ops_data[i][3]
    dur_j = ops_data[j][3]
    # If y_ij = 1 then i finishes before j starts
    model += start[i] + dur_i <= start[j] + M * (1 - y_ij), f"machine_{ops_data[i][2]}_i_before_j_{i}_{j}"
    # If y_ij = 0 then j finishes before i starts
    model += start[j] + dur_j <= start[i] + M * y_ij, f"machine_{ops_data[i][2]}_j_before_i_{i}_{j}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Optimal makespan: {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")
print("Start times (in same time units as durations):")
for i in sorted(ops_data):
    patient, order, device, dur = ops_data[i]
    print(f"  Patient {patient} – operation {order} (Device {device}, dur {dur}) : start = {pulp.value(start[i]):.2f}")

print("\nDevice orderings (y = 1 means first operation precedes second):")
for (i, j), var in y.items():
    print(f"  Ops {i} → {j} on Device {ops_data[i][2]} : y = {pulp.value(var)}")

        for j in range(i + 1, len(ops_on_equip)):
            op1 = ops_on_equip[i]
            op2 = ops_on_equip[j]
            y[(op1, op2)] = pulp.LpVariable(f"y_{op1}_{op2}",
                                            lowBound=0,
                                            upBound=1,
                                            cat=pulp.LpBinary)

Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Makespan", lowBound=0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimize makespan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimize_makespan"

# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1) Completion of each operation must be before the makespan
for op in operations:
    model += s[op] + proc_time[op] <= Cmax, f"Completion_{op}"

# 2) Precedence constraints inside each patient (order must be respected)
for p, ops in patients.items():
    for idx in range(len(ops) - 1):
        op_cur = (p, idx)
        op_next = (p, idx + 1)
        model += (s[op_next] >= s[op_cur] + proc_time[op_cur],
                  f"Precedence_{p}_{idx}")

# 3) Disjunctive (machine) constraints using binary ordering variables
for (op1, op2), yvar in y.items():
    # If y = 1 then op1 before op2, else op2 before op1
    model += (s[op1] + proc_time[op1] <= s[op2] + M * (1 - yvar),
              f"Machine_{machine[op1]}_{op1}_before_{op2}")

              f"Machine_{machine[op2]}_{op2}_before_{op1}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output results
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Status: {status}")
if status == "Optimal":
    print(f"Optimal makespan: {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")
    # Print schedule sorted by start time
    schedule = [(op, pulp.value(s[op]), proc_time[op], machine[op])
                for op in operations]
    schedule.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])  # sort by start time
    print("Schedule (Patient, OperationIndex) : Start  Duration  Equipment")
    for op, start, dur, equip in schedule:
        print(f"  {op} : {start:6.2f}   {dur:8}   {equip}")
else:
    print("No optimal solution found.")
