# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Optimal allocation of computational loads from servers (S) to processing nodes (P)
to minimize total network latency.

The model is a classic transportation problem:
    • Decision variables   x[s][p] = amount of load sent from server s to node p
    • Objective            Minimize Σ latency[s][p] * x[s][p]
    • Supply constraints   Σ_p x[s][p] ≤ capacity_s   for every server s
    • Demand constraints   Σ_s x[s][p] = demand_p     for every node p
All variables are continuous and non‑negative (loads can be split).
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
servers = ["S1", "S2", "S3", "S4", "S5", "S6"]
nodes   = ["P1", "P2", "P3", "P4", "P5", "P6"]

capacity = {
    "S1": 124,
    "S2": 58,
    "S3": 109,
    "S4": 123,
    "S5": 122,
    "S6": 166,
}

demand = {
    "P1": 36,
    "P2": 41,
    "P3": 120,
    "P4": 89,
    "P5": 122,
    "P6": 30,
}

latency = {
    ("S1", "P1"): 4,  ("S1", "P2"): 18, ("S1", "P3"): 8,  ("S1", "P4"): 5,  ("S1", "P5"): 9,  ("S1", "P6"): 5,
    ("S2", "P1"): 3,  ("S2", "P2"): 2,  ("S2", "P3"): 6,  ("S2", "P4"): 10, ("S2", "P5"): 20, ("S2", "P6"): 19,
    ("S3", "P1"): 10, ("S3", "P2"): 15, ("S3", "P3"): 4,  ("S3", "P4"): 15, ("S3", "P5"): 10, ("S3", "P6"): 13,
    ("S4", "P1"): 9,  ("S4", "P2"): 17, ("S4", "P3"): 18, ("S4", "P4"): 16, ("S4", "P5"): 15, ("S4", "P6"): 3,
    ("S5", "P1"): 20, ("S5", "P2"): 2,  ("S5", "P3"): 14, ("S5", "P4"): 11, ("S5", "P5"): 20, ("S5", "P6"): 9,
    ("S6", "P1"): 1,  ("S6", "P2"): 3,  ("S6", "P3"): 8,  ("S6", "P4"): 19, ("S6", "P5"): 19, ("S6", "P6"): 1,
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Latency_Minimization", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: amount shipped from server s to node p
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    ((s, p) for s in servers for p in nodes),
    lowBound=0,
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous,
)

# Objective: minimize total latency
model += pulp.lpSum(latency[(s, p)] * x[(s, p)] for s in servers for p in nodes), "Total_Latency"

# Supply constraints (capacity of each server)
for s in servers:
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(x[(s, p)] for p in nodes) <= capacity[s],
        f"Supply_{s}",
    )

# Demand constraints (required load at each node)
for p in nodes:
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(x[(s, p)] for s in servers) == demand[p],
        f"Demand_{p}",
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output results
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Minimum total latency: {pulp.value(model.objective):.2f}\n")

print("Optimal allocation (units of load from server → node):")
for s in servers:
    for p in nodes:
        qty = x[(s, p)].varValue
        if qty is not None and qty > 1e-6:   # display only positive shipments
            print(f"  {s} → {p} : {qty:.2f}")

# Verify that all demands are met (optional sanity check)
print("\nDemand verification:")
for p in nodes:
    received = sum(x[(s, p)].varValue for s in servers)
    print(f"  {p}: required {demand[p]}, received {received:.2f}")

Data:

    Latency per unit workload from each centre to each node

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sets
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
centres = ["C1", "C2", "C3", "C4", "C5"]
nodes   = ["D1", "D2", "D3", "D4", "D5"]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parameters
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
capacity = {
    "C1": 130,
    "C2": 80,
    "C3": 187,
    "C4": 97,
    "C5": 99,
}

demand = {
    "D1": 65,
    "D2": 97,
    "D3": 131,
    "D4": 70,
    "D5": 37,
}

latency = {
    ("C1", "D1"): 4,  ("C1", "D2"): 7,  ("C1", "D3"): 10, ("C1", "D4"): 8,  ("C1", "D5"): 12,
    ("C2", "D1"): 6,  ("C2", "D2"): 10, ("C2", "D3"): 1,  ("C2", "D4"): 18, ("C2", "D5"): 5,
    ("C3", "D1"): 9,  ("C3", "D2"): 2,  ("C3", "D3"): 2,  ("C3", "D4"): 18, ("C3", "D5"): 10,
    ("C4", "D1"): 5,  ("C4", "D2"): 16, ("C4", "D3"): 4,  ("C4", "D4"): 1,  ("C4", "D5"): 19,
    ("C5", "D1"): 10, ("C5", "D2"): 16, ("C5", "D3"): 16, ("C5", "D4"): 15, ("C5", "D5"): 11,
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    ((i, j) for i in centres for j in nodes),
    lowBound=0,
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous,
)

model += pulp.lpSum(latency[i, j] * x[(i, j)] for i in centres for j in nodes), "Total_Latency"

Optimal personnel assignment (transportation problem)

- 10 regional offices (R1‑R10) with given supplies
- 10 project sites (P1‑P10) with exact demand requirements
- Unit assignment costs are given in the table below
- Objective: minimise total cost
- Variables are integer (number of persons), non‑negative

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

regions = ["R1", "R2", "R3", "R4", "R5", "R6", "R7", "R8", "R9", "R10"]

# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

    ("Alpha",    66),

    ("Delta",    56),
    ("Epsilon",  62),

    ("Xi",       60),
    ("Omicron",  41),
    ("Pi",       59),
    ("Rho",      65),
    ("Sigma",    51),
    ("Tau",      38),
    ("Upsilon",  56),
    ("Phi",      46),
    ("Chi",      54),
]

# Number of items = an upper bound on the number of crates needed
num_items = len(items)

# Create separate index collections for readability
item_ids = [i for i, _ in enumerate(items)]          # 0 … 21
crate_ids = [k for k in range(num_items)]           # at most one crate per item

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("ShippingCrates", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
# x[i][k] = 1 if item i is placed in crate k, else 0
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    (item_ids, crate_ids),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# y[k] = 1 if crate k is used, else 0
y = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "y",
    crate_ids,
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise the number of crates used
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += pulp.lpSum(y[k] for k in crate_ids), "MinCrates"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Every item must be assigned to exactly one crate
for i in item_ids:
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(x[i][k] for k in crate_ids) == 1,
        f"AssignItem_{i}",
    )

# 2. Capacity of each crate (100 kg) must not be exceeded
capacity = 100
for k in crate_ids:
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(items[i][1] * x[i][k] for i in item_ids) <= capacity * y[k],
        f"Capacity_{k}",
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print("Status :", pulp.LpStatus[model.status])
print("Minimum number of crates required :", int(pulp.value(model.objective)))

# Build a readable assignment list
assignments = {}
for k in crate_ids:
    if pulp.value(y[k]) > 0.5:          # crate is used
        assignments[k] = []

for i in item_ids:
    for k in crate_ids:
        if pulp.value(x[i][k]) > 0.5:
            assignments[k].append(items[i][0])
            break

for k, box_list in assignments.items():
    print(f"Crate {k+1}: {', '.join(box_list)}")

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Bin‑packing model for the parcel‑to‑truck allocation problem.
Uses PuLP with the HiGHS solver.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
parcel_names = [
    "Alpha",   "Bravo",   "Charlie", "Delta",   "Echo",
    "Foxtrot", "Golf",    "Hotel",   "India",   "Juliet",
    "Kilo",    "Lima",    "Mike",    "November","Oscar",
    "Papa",    "Quebec",  "Romeo"
]

parcel_weights = [
    47, 61, 55, 30, 49,
    63, 48, 65, 60, 32,
    64, 66, 65, 46, 32,
    59, 55, 37
]

capacity = 100                     # truck capacity (kg)

# Upper bound on the number of trucks.
# A trivial bound is one truck per parcel; a tighter bound is the
# ceiling of total weight / capacity plus a small safety margin.
total_weight = sum(parcel_weights)
min_trucks = (total_weight + capacity - 1) // capacity   # lower bound
max_trucks = len(parcel_names)                           # trivial upper bound
# give a little breathing room (often useful for the solver)
max_trucks = max(min_trucks + 2, max_trucks)

truck_indices = list(range(max_trucks))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Parcel_Truck_Allocation", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
# x[i][k] = 1 if parcel i is placed on truck k, else 0
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    ((i, k) for i in range(len(parcel_names)) for k in truck_indices),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# y[k] = 1 if truck k is used, else 0
y = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "y",
    (k for k in truck_indices),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# Objective: minimise the number of trucks used
model += pulp.lpSum(y[k] for k in truck_indices), "Minimize_trucks"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Every parcel must be assigned to exactly one truck
for i in range(len(parcel_names)):
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[i, k] for k in truck_indices) == 1, f"AssignParcel_{i}"

# 2) The total weight on each truck cannot exceed its capacity
for k in truck_indices:
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(parcel_weights[i] * x[i, k] for i in range(len(parcel_names)))
        <= capacity * y[k],
        f"CapacityTruck_{k}",
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Solver status: {status}")

if status == "Optimal":
    used_trucks = [k for k in truck_indices if pulp.value(y[k]) > 0.5]
    print(f"Number of trucks used: {len(used_trucks)}\n")

    for k in used_trucks:
        assigned = [
            parcel_names[i]
            for i in range(len(parcel_names))
            if pulp.value(x[i, k]) > 0.5
        ]
        weight = sum(parcel_weights[i] for i in range(len(parcel_names)) if pulp.value(x[i, k]) > 0.5)
        print(f"Truck {k+1} (total {weight} kg): {', '.join(assigned)}")
else:
    print("No optimal solution found.")

"""
Bin‑packing model for allocating parcels to identical trucks (capacity 100 kg)
and minimizing the number of trucks used.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
parcel_names = [
    "Alpha", "Bravo", "Charlie", "Delta", "Echo", "Foxtrot", "Golf", "Hotel",
    "India", "Juliet", "Kilo", "Lima", "Mike", "November", "Oscar", "Papa",
    "Quebec", "Romeo"
]

parcel_weights = [
    47, 61, 55, 30, 49, 63, 48, 65,
    60, 32, 64, 66, 65, 46, 32, 59,
    55, 37
]

# sanity check
assert len(parcel_names) == len(parcel_weights)
num_items = len(parcel_names)

# Upper bound on the number of trucks = one truck per parcel (worst case)
max_trucks = num_items

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Truck_Minimisation", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables:
#   x[i][k] = 1 if parcel i is placed in truck k, else 0
#   y[k]    = 1 if truck k is used, else 0
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "assign",
    ((i, k) for i in range(num_items) for k in range(max_trucks)),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

y = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "truck_used",
    (k for k in range(max_trucks)),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# Objective: minimise the number of trucks used
model += pulp.lpSum(y[k] for k in range(max_trucks)), "Minimise_trucks"

# Constraint 1: each parcel assigned to exactly one truck
for i in range(num_items):
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(i, k)] for k in range(max_trucks)) == 1, f"Assign_{parcel_names[i]}"

# Constraint 2: capacity of each truck (if truck not used, no weight can be assigned)
capacity = 100
for k in range(max_trucks):
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(parcel_weights[i] * x[(i, k)] for i in range(num_items))
        <= capacity * y[k]
    ), f"Capacity_{k}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Solution status: {status}")

if status == "Optimal":
    trucks_used = [k for k in range(max_trucks) if pulp.value(y[k]) > 0.5]
    print(f"Minimum number of trucks required: {len(trucks_used)}\n")

    # Build a readable assignment per truck
    assignments = {k: [] for k in trucks_used}
    for i in range(num_items):
        for k in trucks_used:
            if pulp.value(x[(i, k)]) > 0.5:
                assignments[k].append(parcel_names[i])
                break

    for k in sorted(assignments):
        assigned_parcels = assignments[k]
        total_weight = sum(parcel_weights[parcel_names.index(p)] for p in assigned_parcels)
        print(f"Truck {k + 1}:")
        print(f"  Parcels: {', '.join(assigned_parcels)}")
        print(f"  Total weight: {total_weight} kg\n")
else:
    print("No optimal solution found.")

]                                   # item i weight (kg)

max_capacity = 100                 # pallet capacity (kg)

# pallets than items, so we use N = num_items.
num_pallets = num_items

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Decision variables
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# x[i][k] = 1 if item i is placed on pallet k, 0 otherwise
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    ((i, k) for i in range(num_items) for k in range(num_pallets)),

    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

    "y",
    (k for k in range(num_pallets)),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("MinPallets", pulp.LpMinimize)

model += pulp.lpSum(y[k] for k in range(num_pallets)), "TotalPallets"

        pulp.lpSum(x[(i, k)] for k in range(num_pallets)) == 1,

    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(weights[i] * x[(i, k)] for i in range(num_items))
        <= max_capacity * y[k],
        f"Capacity_{k}",
    )

weights = [
    34, 45, 34, 43, 43, 68, 42, 52, 53, 30,
    49, 47, 30, 51, 69, 33, 52, 40, 56, 35,
    57, 65, 39, 59, 60, 64, 50, 30, 53, 31,
    35, 59, 61, 30, 45, 63
]                      # index 0 … 35  (36 items)

capacity = 100          # pallet capacity (kg)
num_items = len(weights)

# Upper bound on the number of pallets = one pallet per item (worst case)
max_pallets = num_items

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
model = pulp.LpProblem("PalletPacking", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
# x[i][k] = 1 if item i is placed on pallet k, else 0
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "x",
    (range(num_items), range(max_pallets)),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# y[k] = 1 if pallet k is used, else 0
y = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "y",
    range(max_pallets),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise total number of pallets used
model += pulp.lpSum(y[k] for k in range(max_pallets)), "MinPallets"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints

# 1) Every item must be assigned to exactly one pallet
for i in range(num_items):
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(x[i][k] for k in range(max_pallets)) == 1,
        f"AssignItem_{i}",
    )

# 2) Capacity of each pallet cannot be exceeded
for k in range(max_pallets):
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(weights[i] * x[i][k] for i in range(num_items))
        <= capacity * y[k],
        f"Capacity_{k}",
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output results
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Solver status: {status}")

        items_str = ", ".join(map(str, pallet_contents[k]))
        print(f"Pallet {k + 1}: items [{items_str}]  total weight = {pallet_weights[k]} kg")
else:
    print("No optimal solution found.")

}

    "x",

    lowBound=0,

    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

    "y",
    (k for k in range(max_bins)),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# x[i,j] = 1 if parcel i is placed on truck j, 0 otherwise

for i in range(num_trucks):
    for j in range(num_trucks):
        var_name = f"x_{i}_{j}"
        x[(i, j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")

y = {}
for j in range(num_trucks):

"""
Bin‑packing model for allocating fragile equipment crates to pallets.
Each pallet can carry at most 100 mass units.
The model minimizes the number of pallets used.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
crate_names = [
    "Alpha", "Beta", "Gamma", "Delta", "Epsilon", "Zeta", "Eta",
    "Theta", "Iota", "Kappa", "Lambda", "Mu", "Nu", "Xi", "Omicron"
]

crate_masses = {
    "Alpha":   52,
    "Beta":    59,
    "Gamma":   70,
    "Delta":   70,
    "Epsilon": 35,
    "Zeta":    60,
    "Eta":     43,
    "Theta":   48,
    "Iota":    30,
    "Kappa":   58,
    "Lambda":  69,
    "Mu":      59,
    "Nu":      30,
    "Xi":      43,
    "Omicron": 49
}

# Upper bound on the number of pallets (worst case: one crate per pallet)
max_pallets = len(crate_names)          # 15

pallet_ids = list(range(max_pallets))   # 0 … 14

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Pallet_Allocation", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
# x[(c,p)] = 1 if crate c is placed on pallet p, else 0
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "assign",
    ((c, p) for c in crate_names for p in pallet_ids),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# y[p] = 1 if pallet p is used, else 0
y = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "pallet_used",
    (p for p in pallet_ids),
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=1,
    cat=pulp.LpBinary,
)

# Objective: minimise total number of pallets used
model += pulp.lpSum(y[p] for p in pallet_ids), "Minimize_number_of_pallets"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Every crate must be assigned to exactly one pallet
for c in crate_names:
    model += pulp.lpSum(x[(c, p)] for p in pallet_ids) == 1, f"Assign_{c}_once"

# 2) Capacity of each pallet must not exceed 100 mass units
capacity = 100
for p in pallet_ids:
    model += (
        pulp.lpSum(crate_masses[c] * x[(c, p)] for c in crate_names)
        <= capacity * y[p]
    ), f"Capacity_pallet_{p}"

# 3) Linking constraint (implicit in capacity): a pallet can only carry crates if it is "used"
#    (already enforced by the capacity constraint because y[p] = 0 forces all x[(c,p)] = 0)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Solver status: {status}")

if status == "Optimal":
    used_pallets = [p for p in pallet_ids if pulp.value(y[p]) > 0.5]
    print(f"Minimum number of pallets required: {len(used_pallets)}\n")

    # Build a readable assignment dictionary
    assignment = {p: [] for p in used_pallets}
    for c in crate_names:
        for p in used_pallets:
            if pulp.value(x[(c, p)]) > 0.5:
                assignment[p].append(c)
                break

    for p in sorted(assignment):
        crates_on_p = assignment[p]
        total_mass = sum(crate_masses[c] for c in crates_on_p)
        print(f"Pallet {p + 1}:")
        print(f"  Crates: {', '.join(crates_on_p)}")
        print(f"  Total mass: {total_mass} / {capacity}\n")
else:
    print("No optimal solution found.")

"""
Optimal procurement and storage plan for a maritime fuel additive
using PuLP with the HiGHS solver.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
T = 20                                 # number of port calls / legs
capacity = 37.0                        # tank capacity (kL)
init_stock = 13.0                      # initial stock at departure (kL)

# demand (consumption) for each leg, indexed from 1
demand = {
    1: 55.0, 2: 26.0, 3: 22.0, 4: 41.0, 5: 40.0,
    6: 26.0, 7: 42.0, 8: 35.0, 9: 18.0,10: 48.0,
   11: 41.0,12: 27.0,13: 21.0,14: 54.0,15: 10.0,
   16: 23.0,17: 31.0,18: 26.0,19: 55.0,20: 55.0
}

procurement_cost = 3.0   # per kL ordered
holding_cost     = 3.0   # per kL kept from one leg to the next
shortage_penalty = 9.0   # per kL of unmet consumption
max_order = 47.0         # maximum order size per port call
lead_time = 2            # lead time in port calls

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Additive_Procurement_and_Storage", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
# x[t] : quantity ordered at port call t (kL)
x = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("order",
                          (t for t in range(1, T+1)),
                          lowBound=0,
                          upBound=max_order,
                          cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# S[t] : inventory level at the end of leg t (kL)
# we also need S[0] for the initial stock
S = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("stock",
                          (t for t in range(0, T+1)),
                          lowBound=0,
                          upBound=capacity,
                          cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# u[t] : unmet demand (shortage) at leg t (kL)
u = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("shortage",
                          (t for t in range(1, T+1)),
                          lowBound=0,
                          cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Initial stock
model += S[0] == init_stock, "Initial_Stock"

# Inventory balance with lead time
for t in range(1, T+1):
    # arrivals from orders placed lead_time periods earlier
    if t - lead_time >= 1:
        arrivals = x[t - lead_time]
    else:
        arrivals = 0.0

    # Balance equation:
    # stock at end of period t = stock at end of period t-1
    #                           + arrivals
    #                           - demand[t]
    #                           + shortage[t]
    model += (S[t] == S[t-1] + arrivals - demand[t] + u[t],
              f"Balance_{t}")

# No explicit upper bound on shortage; it is naturally limited by demand
# (the model will never order more than needed because of costs).

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
procurement_term = pulp.lpSum(procurement_cost * x[t] for t in range(1, T+1))
holding_term    = pulp.lpSum(holding_cost * S[t]   for t in range(1, T+1))
shortage_term   = pulp.lpSum(shortage_penalty * u[t] for t in range(1, T+1))

model += procurement_term + holding_term + shortage_term, "Total_Cost"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output results
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Total Cost: {pulp.value(model.objective):.2f}\n")

print("Period | Order (kL) | End-Stock (kL) | Shortage (kL)")
print("-"*50)
for t in range(1, T+1):

over a 10‑day horizon.

Decision variables (continuous):
  pump[t]      – gallons pumped from the aquifer on day t (9 ≤ pump ≤ 76)
  storage[t]   – reservoir volume at the end of day t (0 ≤ storage ≤ 39)
  short[t]     – unmet demand on day t (0 ≤ short ≤ demand)

  Minimize total cost = Σ_t (6·pump[t] + 3·storage[t] + 14·short[t])

Constraints for each day t = 1,…,10:
  storage[t] = storage[t‑1] + pump[t] – demand[t] + short[t]
  (water balance)

Parameters are entered directly from the problem statement.
"""

import pulp

# -----------------------------
# Data
# -----------------------------
T = range(1, 11)                     # days 1..10
initial_storage = 27.0               # million gallons at start
capacity = 39.0                      # reservoir capacity

demand = {
    1: 11.0,
    2: 17.0,
    3: 49.0,
    4: 60.0,
    5: 55.0,
    6: 16.0,
    7: 21.0,
    8: 56.0,
    9: 36.0,
    10: 25.0,
}

pump_min = 9.0
pump_max = 76.0

cost_pump = 6.0      # per million gallons pumped
cost_storage = 3.0   # per million gallons stored overnight
cost_short = 14.0    # per million gallons of unmet demand

# -----------------------------
# Model
# -----------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Reservoir_Pumping_Schedule", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
pump = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("pump", T, lowBound=pump_min, upBound=pump_max, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)
storage = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("storage", T, lowBound=0.0, upBound=capacity, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)
short = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("short", T, lowBound=0.0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

for t in T:
    model += short[t] <= demand[t], f"ShortageCap_day{t}"

for t in T:

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Optimal weekly procurement‑storage plan for a water‑treatment facility
using PuLP (HiGHS solver).

The model follows the description:

* 12 weekly periods (t = 1 … 12)
* Initial on‑site inventory = 19 kL
* Order each week must be between 18 and 44 kL
* Orders arrive after a 2‑week lag
* Weekly demand is given (kL)
* Unmet demand (shortage) is allowed, incurs a penalty
* Inventory cannot exceed 59 kL
* Costs:
    - Procurement: 4 per kL ordered
    - Holding:    1 per kL held at the end of a week
    - Shortage:  14 per kL unmet
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
weeks = range(1, 13)                     # 1 … 12
demand = {
    1: 45,
    2: 30,
    3: 31,
    4: 22,
    5: 55,
    6: 60,
    7: 37,
    8: 60,
    9: 19,
    10: 10,
    11: 58,
    12: 42,
}
initial_inventory = 19.0
order_lb, order_ub = 18.0, 44.0          # allowed order range each week
inventory_cap = 59.0

procurement_cost = 4.0
holding_cost = 1.0
shortage_cost = 14.0

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Water_Treatment_Procurement", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
order = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "order", weeks, lowBound=order_lb, upBound=order_ub, cat=pulp.LpContinuous
)

# inventory indexed 0 … 12 (inventory[0] is the initial stock)
inventory = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "inventory", range(0, 13), lowBound=0, upBound=inventory_cap, cat=pulp.LpContinuous
)

shortage = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "shortage", weeks, lowBound=0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous
)

# Initial inventory
model += inventory[0] == initial_inventory, "Initial_Inventory"

# Flow balance and shortage limits for each week
for t in weeks:
    # Arrival in week t: order placed two weeks earlier
    if t >= 3:
        arrival = order[t - 2]
    else:
        arrival = 0.0

    # Inventory balance:
    # inv_t = inv_{t-1} + arrival - (demand_t - shortage_t)
    model += (
        inventory[t]
        == inventory[t - 1] + arrival - demand[t] + shortage[t],
        f"Balance_Week_{t}",
    )

    # Shortage cannot exceed the weekly demand
    model += shortage[t] <= demand[t], f"Shortage_Limit_Week_{t}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise total cost (procurement + holding + shortage)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
total_cost = pulp.lpSum(
    procurement_cost * order[t] + holding_cost * inventory[t] + shortage_cost * shortage[t]
    for t in weeks
)
model += total_cost, "Total_Cost"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Solver status: {status}")

if status == "Optimal":
    print("\nOptimal weekly decisions")
    print("-" * 40)
    print(f"{'Week':>4} | {'Order(kL)':>10} | {'Arrival(kL)':>11} | {'Inv_end(kL)':>11} | {'Shortage(kL)':>12}")
    print("-" * 40)
    for t in weeks:
        ord_val = order[t].varValue
        arr_val = order[t - 2].varValue if t >= 3 else 0.0
        inv_val = inventory[t].varValue
        sh_val = shortage[t].varValue

    print(f"Total shortage cost   : {shortage_cost * sum(shortage[t].varValue for t in weeks):.2f}")
    print(f"Overall total cost    : {pulp.value(model.objective):.2f}")
else:

)

    "inv_0", lowBound=initial_stock, upBound=initial_stock, cat=pulp.LpContinuous
)

    inventory[t] = pulp.LpVariable(
        f"inv_{t}",
        lowBound=0.0,
        upBound=storage_capacity,
        cat=pulp.LpContinuous,
    )

    "shortage",

    lowBound=0.0,

)

    model += (

        == demand[t] + shortage[t] + inventory[t],

storage_capacity = 59          # maximum inventory allowed

storage_cost = 1               # $ per kiloliter held from week t to t+1
shortage_penalty = 14          # $ per kiloliter of unmet demand
lead_time = 2                  # weeks between order and arrival

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Reagent_Procurement_and_Storage", pulp.LpMinimize)

    "Order",
    weeks,
    lowBound=order_min,
    upBound=order_max,
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous,
)

inventory = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "Inv",
    weeks,
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=storage_capacity,
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous,
)

# Shortage (unmet demand) in each week (continuous, cannot exceed demand)
shortage = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "Short",
    weeks,
    lowBound=0,
    upBound=None,
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous,
)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

    procurement_cost * order[t]
    + storage_cost * inventory[t]
    + shortage_penalty * shortage[t]
    for t in weeks
), "Total_Cost"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Shortage cannot be larger than the weekly demand
for t in weeks:
    model += shortage[t] <= demand[t], f"Shortage_UpperBound_Week{t}"

# 2. Inventory balance with a 2‑week lead time
#    I_t = I_{t-1} + arrival_t - demand_t + shortage_t
#    arrival_t = order_{t-2}  (0 if t-2 < 1)

# we also create I[0] to fix the initial stock

------------------

stock[t]: continuous, water volume in the reservoir at the end of day t (ML),
          0 ≤ stock[t] ≤ 63
short[t]: continuous, unmet demand on day t (ML), 0 ≤ short[t] ≤ demand[t]

Objective
---------
minimise  Σ_t ( 6·p[t] + 1·stock[t] + 13·short[t] )

Constraints
-----------

      p[t] ≥ 2·y[t] ,  p[t] ≤ 42·y[t]          ∀ t
* Reservoir dynamics (lag = 2 days):
      inflow[t] = p[t‑2]   if t > 2 else 0
      stock[t] = stock[t‑1] + inflow[t] – ( demand[t] – short[t] )
* Shortfall cannot exceed demand:
      short[t] ≤ demand[t]                     ∀ t
* Initial stock:
      stock[0] = 63 (given as a parameter)
"""

import pulp

# -------------------------- data ---------------------------------
T = 11                                   # planning horizon (days)
initial_stock = 63.0                     # ML, stock at start of day 1
capacity = 63.0                          # ML, maximum reservoir volume
pump_min = 2.0                           # ML, min pumped when station is on
pump_max = 42.0                          # ML, max pumped when station is on
lag = 2                                  # days
pump_cost = 6.0                          # $/ML
storage_cost = 1.0                       # $/ML per night
shortage_penalty = 13.0                  # $/ML unmet demand

# daily demand (ML)
demand = {
    1: 49, 2: 48, 3: 12, 4: 26, 5: 31,
    6: 57, 7: 56, 8: 34, 9: 11, 10: 50, 11: 12
}

# -------------------------- model --------------------------------

# decision variables
pump = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("pump", range(1, T + 1), lowBound=0, upBound=pump_max, cat="Continuous")
pump_on = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("pump_on", range(1, T + 1), cat="Binary")
stock = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("stock", range(1, T + 1), lowBound=0, upBound=capacity, cat="Continuous")
short = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("short", range(1, T + 1), lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

for t in range(1, T + 1):
    model += pump[t] >= pump_min * pump_on[t], f"PumpMin_day{t}"
    model += pump[t] <= pump_max * pump_on[t], f"PumpMax_day{t}"

    storage_cost * stock[t] +

)
model += obj, "TotalCost"

Model:

        - order[t]   : quantity ordered in week t (continuous, 0 ≤ order[t] ≤ 42)
        - inv[t]     : inventory on hand at the end of week t (continuous, 0 ≤ inv[t] ≤ 88)

        - C_short    = 9   (penalty per dose of unmet demand)

        inv[t] = inv[t‑1] + arrivals[t] – demand[t] + short[t]

        where arrivals[t] = order[t‑2] if t‑2 ≥ 1, otherwise 0.

    • Objective (to be minimized)
        total_cost =  C_order  * Σ order[t]
                    + C_hold   * (init_stock + Σ_{t=1}^{7} inv[t])
                    + C_short  * Σ short[t]

The model is a linear program with continuous variables.
"""

import pulp

# -------------------------
# 1. Data
# -------------------------
weeks = range(1, 9)                     # weeks 1..8
demand = {
    1: 30,
    2: 56,
    3: 26,
    4: 15,
    5: 32,
    6: 14,
    7: 17,
    8: 32,
}
init_stock = 88
order_min, order_max = 0, 42
capacity = 88

# -------------------------
# 2. Model definition
# -------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Vaccine_Procurement_and_Inventory", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
order = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("order", weeks, lowBound=order_min, upBound=order_max, cat="Continuous")
inv   = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("inv",   weeks, lowBound=0,          upBound=capacity, cat="Continuous")
short = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("short", weeks, lowBound=0,          upBound=None,    cat="Continuous")

# -------------------------
# 3. Constraints
# -------------------------

# Inventory balance for each week
for t in weeks:
    # arrivals from orders placed two weeks earlier
    if t - 2 >= 1:
        arrivals = order[t - 2]
    else:
        arrivals = 0

r = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("request", T, lowBound=18, upBound=74, cat="Continuous")
a = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("arrival", T, lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

u = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("unmet", T, lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

"""
Job‑shop scheduling model for 5 products (jobs) and 5 stations (machines).

Each product must follow a fixed sequence of operations.
The model minimizes the makespan (total completion time).

The model is built with PuLP and solved by the HiGHS MILP solver.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Jobs are indexed 1..5, operations within a job are indexed 1..5
jobs = {
    1: [("B", 1), ("E", 2), ("D", 7), ("A", 5), ("C", 2)],
    2: [("E", 4), ("C", 2), ("A", 9), ("B", 5), ("D", 6)],
    3: [("B",10), ("C", 3), ("D", 3), ("E", 1), ("A", 9)],
    4: [("E", 7), ("C", 3), ("B", 3), ("A", 9), ("D", 2)],
    5: [("B", 3), ("E", 4), ("D", 7), ("A", 6), ("C",10)]
}

machines = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]

# Helper: total processing time (used for a big‑M constant)
bigM = sum(dur for ops in jobs.values() for (_, dur) in ops)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("JobShop", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: start time of each operation (continuous, >=0)
start = {}
for j, ops in jobs.items():
    for o, (m, p) in enumerate(ops, start=1):
        var = pulp.LpVariable(f"s_{j}_{o}", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")
        start[(j, o)] = var

# Makespan variable
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Binary ordering variables for every unordered pair of operations that share a machine
# y[(j1,o1,j2,o2)] = 1  => operation (j1,o1) finishes before (j2,o2) starts
order = {}
for m in machines:
    # collect all operations that require machine m
    ops_on_m = [(j, o, p) for j, ops in jobs.items()
                for o, (mm, p) in enumerate(ops, start=1) if mm == m]
    # create ordering variables for each unordered pair
    for i in range(len(ops_on_m)):
        j1, o1, p1 = ops_on_m[i]
        for j2, o2, p2 in ops_on_m[i+1:]:
            var = pulp.LpVariable(f"y_{j1}_{o1}_{j2}_{o2}", cat="Binary")
            order[(j1, o1, j2, o2)] = var
            # also store the reverse key for convenience (same variable)
            order[(j2, o2, j1, o1)] = var

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Precedence constraints inside each job
for j, ops in jobs.items():
    for o in range(1, len(ops)):
        p = ops[o-1][1]                     # processing time of operation o
        model += (start[(j, o+1)] >= start[(j, o)] + p,
                  f"prec_job{j}_op{o}_to_{o+1}")

# 2) Machine capacity constraints (no overlap on the same machine)
for m in machines:
    # list of operations on this machine
    ops_on_m = [(j, o, p) for j, ops in jobs.items()
                for o, (mm, p) in enumerate(ops, start=1) if mm == m]
    for i in range(len(ops_on_m)):
        j1, o1, p1 = ops_on_m[i]
        for j2, o2, p2 in ops_on_m[i+1:]:
            y = order[(j1, o1, j2, o2)]
            # (j1,o1) before (j2,o2)
            model += (start[(j2, o2)] >= start[(j1, o1)] + p1 - bigM * (1 - y),
                      f"mach_{m}_order_{j1}_{o1}_before_{j2}_{o2}")
            # (j2,o2) before (j1,o1)
            model += (start[(j1, o1)] >= start[(j2, o2)] + p2 - bigM * y,
                      f"mach_{m}_order_{j2}_{o2}_before_{j1}_{o1}")

# 3) Definition of makespan
for j, ops in jobs.items():
    last_op = len(ops)
    p_last = ops[-1][1]
    model += (Cmax >= start[(j, last_op)] + p_last,
              f"makespan_job{j}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimize_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Optimal makespan: {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times (job, operation):")
for j, ops in jobs.items():
    for o in range(1, len(ops)+1):
        print(f"  Job {j} Op {o} (Machine {ops[o-1][0]}, dur {ops[o-1][1]}): "
              f"start = {pulp.value(start[(j, o)])}")

# Optional: a simple Gantt‑like table
print("\nGantt chart (start – finish):")
for j, ops in jobs.items():
    line = f"Job {j}: "
    for o, (m, p) in enumerate(ops, start=1):
        s = pulp.value(start[(j, o)])
        line += f"[{m} {s:.1f}-{s+p:.1f}] "
    print(line)

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Job‑shop scheduling model for 5 products and 5 stations.
Goal: minimise the makespan (total completion time).

Each operation is identified by (product, operation_index) where operation_index
starts at 0 for the first treatment of the product.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Products (jobs) with their ordered list of (station, duration)
jobs_data = {
    1: [("B", 1), ("E", 2), ("D", 7), ("A", 5), ("C", 2)],
    2: [("E", 4), ("C", 2), ("A", 9), ("B", 5), ("D", 6)],
    3: [("B", 10), ("C", 3), ("D", 3), ("E", 1), ("A", 9)],
    4: [("E", 7), ("C", 3), ("B", 3), ("A", 9), ("D", 2)],
    5: [("B", 3), ("E", 4), ("D", 7), ("A", 6), ("C", 10)],
}

# All stations (machines)
stations = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Build operation list
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# op_id -> (job, index, station, proc_time)
ops = {}
op_counter = 0
for job, seq in jobs_data.items():
    for idx, (st, pt) in enumerate(seq):
        ops[op_counter] = {"job": job, "idx": idx, "station": st, "pt": pt}
        op_counter += 1

num_ops = len(ops)

# Helper: map (job, idx) -> op_id
job_idx_to_op = {(v["job"], v["idx"]): k for k, v in ops.items()}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Big‑M (upper bound on any start time)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sum of all processing times is a safe upper bound.
M = sum(v["pt"] for v in ops.values())

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("JobShop_Makespan_Minimisation", pulp.LpMinimize)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Decision variables
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Start time of each operation (continuous, >=0)
S = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("Start", range(num_ops), lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Makespan
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Makespan", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Binary ordering variables for every unordered pair of ops that share a station
Y = {}
for i in range(num_ops):
    for j in range(i + 1, num_ops):
        if ops[i]["station"] == ops[j]["station"]:
            var_name = f"Y_{i}_{j}"
            Y[(i, j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimise_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Job‑precedence constraints (operations within the same product)
for job, seq in jobs_data.items():
    for k in range(len(seq) - 1):
        op_curr = job_idx_to_op[(job, k)]
        op_next = job_idx_to_op[(job, k + 1)]
        model += (
            S[op_next] >= S[op_curr] + ops[op_curr]["pt"],
            f"Precedence_job{job}_op{k}_to_{k+1}",
        )

# 2) Machine capacity (no overlap) using binary ordering variables
for (i, j), y_var in Y.items():
    pi = ops[i]["pt"]
    pj = ops[j]["pt"]
    # i after j  (y = 1)  ->  Si >= Sj + pj
    model += (
        S[i] >= S[j] + pj - M * (1 - y_var),
        f"Machine_{ops[i]['station']}_order_{i}_after_{j}",
    )
    # j after i  (y = 0)  ->  Sj >= Si + pi
    model += (
        S[j] >= S[i] + pi - M * y_var,
        f"Machine_{ops[i]['station']}_order_{j}_after_{i}",
    )

# 3) Definition of makespan
for op_id, data in ops.items():
    model += (
        Cmax >= S[op_id] + data["pt"],
        f"Makespan_def_op{op_id}",
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output results
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
status = pulp.LpStatus[model.status]
print(f"Status: {status}")
print(f"Optimal makespan: {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times (in time units):")
for op_id in range(num_ops):
    start = pulp.value(S[op_id])
    data = ops[op_id]
    print(
        f"Product {data['job']}, operation {data['idx'] + 1} "
        f"(Station {data['station']}, duration {data['pt']}): start = {start}"
    )

# Job‑shop scheduling model for the 5‑product, 5‑station problem
# Solved with PuLP and the HiGHS solver

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
jobs = ["P1", "P2", "P3", "P4", "P5"]
machines = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]

# (machine, processing time) for each operation in the required order
job_operations = {
    "P1": [("B", 1), ("E", 2), ("D", 7), ("A", 5), ("C", 2)],
    "P2": [("E", 4), ("C", 2), ("A", 9), ("B", 5), ("D", 6)],
    "P3": [("B",10), ("C", 3), ("D", 3), ("E", 1), ("A", 9)],
    "P4": [("E", 7), ("C", 3), ("B", 3), ("A", 9), ("D", 2)],
    "P5": [("B", 3), ("E", 4), ("D", 7), ("A", 6), ("C",10)],
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper structures
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Map each (job,op_index) to its machine and processing time
op_machine = {}
op_proc    = {}
for j, ops in job_operations.items():
    for idx, (m, p) in enumerate(ops):
        op = (j, idx)                     # unique identifier
        op_machine[op] = m
        op_proc[op]    = p

# List of all operations
operations = list(op_machine.keys())

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("JobShop", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables: start time of every operation (continuous, >=0)
start = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("Start",
                              ((j, i) for j, i in operations),
                              lowBound=0,
                              cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# Makespan variable
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise makespan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimise_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Precedence constraints inside each job (given order)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for j, ops in job_operations.items():
    for idx in range(len(ops) - 1):
        cur = (j, idx)
        nxt = (j, idx + 1)
        model += (start[nxt] >= start[cur] + op_proc[cur],
                  f"Precedence_{j}_{idx}_to_{idx+1}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) Disjunctive (machine capacity) constraints
#    For every pair of operations that need the same machine we create a binary
#    variable that decides their order.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Upper bound M large enough to separate any two operations
M = sum(op_proc.values()) + 10   # a safe big‑M

# Collect operations per machine
ops_on_machine = {m: [] for m in machines}
for op in operations:
    m = op_machine[op]
    ops_on_machine[m].append(op)

# Binary ordering variables and non‑overlap constraints
order = {}   # (op_i, op_j) -> binary variable, i precedes j if 1
for m, ops in ops_on_machine.items():
    # consider every unordered pair
    for i in range(len(ops)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(ops)):
            op_i = ops[i]
            op_j = ops[j]
            # binary variable: 1 if op_i finishes before op_j starts
            y = pulp.LpVariable(f"Y_{op_i[0]}_{op_i[1]}_before_{op_j[0]}_{op_j[1]}",
                                cat=pulp.LpBinary)
            order[(op_i, op_j)] = y

            # i before j  OR  j before i
            model += (start[op_i] + op_proc[op_i] <= start[op_j] + M * (1 - y),
                      f"Machine_{m}_no_overlap_{op_i}_before_{op_j}")
            model += (start[op_j] + op_proc[op_j] <= start[op_i] + M * y,
                      f"Machine_{m}_no_overlap_{op_j}_before_{op_i}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Definition of makespan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
for j, ops in job_operations.items():
    last_op = (j, len(ops) - 1)
    model += (Cmax >= start[last_op] + op_proc[last_op],
              f"Makespan_def_{j}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Optimal makespan (Cmax): {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times:")
for op in sorted(operations):
    j, idx = op
    print(f"  {j} operation {idx+1} (Machine {op_machine[op]}, "
          f"proc {op_proc[op]}): start = {pulp.value(start[op]):.2f}")

and the HiGHS solver.

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

    # P1
    ("P1", 0): ("B", 1),
    ("P1", 1): ("E", 2),
    ("P1", 2): ("D", 7),
    ("P1", 3): ("A", 5),
    ("P1", 4): ("C", 2),

    ("P2", 2): ("A", 9),
    ("P2", 3): ("B", 5),
    ("P2", 4): ("D", 6),
    # P3
    ("P3", 0): ("B", 10),
    ("P3", 1): ("C", 3),
    ("P3", 2): ("D", 3),
    ("P3", 3): ("E", 1),
    ("P3", 4): ("A", 9),
    # P4
    ("P4", 0): ("E", 7),
    ("P4", 1): ("C", 3),
    ("P4", 2): ("B", 3),
    ("P4", 3): ("A", 9),
    ("P4", 4): ("D", 2),
    # P5
    ("P5", 0): ("B", 3),
    ("P5", 1): ("E", 4),
    ("P5", 2): ("D", 7),
    ("P5", 3): ("A", 6),
    ("P5", 4): ("C", 10),
}

jobs = ["P1", "P2", "P3", "P4", "P5"]
machines = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]

# Create a list of all operation identifiers for easier handling
ops = []
for j in jobs:
    for o in range(5):          # each job has exactly 5 operations
        ops.append((j, o))

# Big‑M value: larger than any possible makespan (sum of all processing times)
big_M = sum(p for (_, p) in operations_data.values())

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("JobShop_Makespan_Minimization", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
# start time of each operation (continuous, >=0)
start = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "Start",
    ((j, o) for (j, o) in ops),
    lowBound=0,
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous,
)

# makespan (continuous, >=0)
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Makespan", lowBound=0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# binary ordering variables for each pair of operations that share a machine
order = {}   # key: (op_i, op_j) with i < j, value: binary variable
for m in machines:
    # collect all operations processed on machine m
    ops_on_m = [(j, o) for (j, o) in ops if operations_data[(j, o)][0] == m]
    # create binary variable for each unordered pair
    for idx in range(len(ops_on_m)):
        for jdx in range(idx + 1, len(ops_on_m)):
            op_i = ops_on_m[idx]
            op_j = ops_on_m[jdx]
            var = pulp.LpVariable(f"Y_{op_i[0]}_{op_i[1]}_before_{op_j[0]}_{op_j[1]}", cat=pulp.LpBinary)
            order[(op_i, op_j)] = var

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimize_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Completion of each job's last operation is bounded by makespan
for j in jobs:
    last_op = (j, 4)          # 5th operation (index 4)
    proc_time = operations_data[last_op][1]
    model += start[last_op] + proc_time <= Cmax, f"Makespan_bound_{j}"

# 2) Precedence constraints inside each job
for j in jobs:
    for o in range(4):        # 0..3, each must precede the next
        cur = (j, o)
        nxt = (j, o + 1)
        cur_time = operations_data[cur][1]
        model += start[nxt] >= start[cur] + cur_time, f"Precedence_{j}_{o}_to_{o+1}"

# 3) Disjunctive (machine capacity) constraints using ordering binaries
for ((i_job, i_op), (j_job, j_op)), y_ij in order.items():
    # retrieve processing times
    p_i = operations_data[(i_job, i_op)][1]
    p_j = operations_data[(j_job, j_op)][1]

    # i before j  ->  start_i + p_i <= start_j   (when y_ij = 1)
    model += start[(i_job, i_op)] + p_i <= start[(j_job, j_op)] + big_M * (1 - y_ij), \
        f"Machine_{operations_data[(i_job, i_op)][0]}_order1_{i_job}{i_op}_{j_job}{j_op}"

    # j before i  ->  start_j + p_j <= start_i   (when y_ij = 0)
    model += start[(j_job, j_op)] + p_j <= start[(i_job, i_op)] + big_M * y_ij, \
        f"Machine_{operations_data[(i_job, i_op)][0]}_order2_{i_job}{i_op}_{j_job}{j_op}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print("Status:", pulp.LpStatus[model.status])
print("Optimal makespan:", pulp.value(Cmax))
print("\nStart times:")
for (j, o) in ops:
    s = pulp.value(start[(j, o)])
    m, p = operations_data[(j, o)]
    print(f"  Job {j} Op{o+1} (Machine {m}, dur {p}): start = {s:.2f}")

        op_machine[(j, idx)] = m
        op_time[(j, idx)]    = t

# Upper bound for the big‑M (larger than any possible makespan)
M = sum(op_time[o] for o in ops) + 10   # 123+10 = 133, safe enough

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("JobShop", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
# start time of each operation (continuous, >=0)
start = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "Start",
    ((j, idx) for (j, idx) in ops),
    lowBound=0,
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous,
)

# makespan (continuous)
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Makespan", lowBound=0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# Binary variables that decide the order of any two operations that share a machine
order = {}
for i in range(len(ops)):
    for k in range(i + 1, len(ops)):
        job_i, idx_i = ops[i]
        job_k, idx_k = ops[k]
        if op_machine[(job_i, idx_i)] == op_machine[(job_k, idx_k)]:
            # create a binary variable y_{i,k} == 1  => operation i precedes operation k
            var = pulp.LpVariable(f"Y_{job_i}{idx_i}_{job_k}{idx_k}", cat=pulp.LpBinary)
            order[(job_i, idx_i, job_k, idx_k)] = var

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimise_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Completion of each operation must be before makespan
for (j, idx) in ops:
    model += start[(j, idx)] + op_time[(j, idx)] <= Cmax, f"Completion_{j}_{idx}"

# 2) Precedence constraints inside each job (the given order must be respected)
for j in jobs:
    num_ops = len(products[j])
    for idx in range(num_ops - 1):
        model += (
            start[(j, idx + 1)] >= start[(j, idx)] + op_time[(j, idx)],
            f"Precedence_{j}_{idx}_to_{idx+1}",
        )

# 3) Disjunctive (machine capacity) constraints using the binary order variables
for (j1, i1, j2, i2), y in order.items():
    # operation (j1,i1) before (j2,i2)
    model += (
        start[(j1, i1)] + op_time[(j1, i1)] <= start[(j2, i2)] + M * (1 - y),
        f"Machine_{op_machine[(j1,i1)]}_order1_{j1}{i1}_{j2}{i2}",
    )
    # operation (j2,i2) before (j1,i1)
    model += (
        start[(j2, i2)] + op_time[(j2, i2)] <= start[(j1, i1)] + M * y,
        f"Machine_{op_machine[(j1,i1)]}_order2_{j1}{i1}_{j2}{i2}",
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Optimal makespan: {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times (in the optimal schedule):")
for j in jobs:
    for idx in range(len(products[j])):
        st = pulp.value(start[(j, idx)])
        m  = op_machine[(j, idx)]
        dur = op_time[(j, idx)]
        print(f"  {j} - Op{idx+1} (Station {m}, dur {dur}): start = {st:.2f}")

print("\nMachine sequences:")
for m in machines:

    ops_on_m = [(j, idx) for (j, idx) in ops if op_machine[(j, idx)] == m]
    # sort by start time

# Job‑shop scheduling for 5 products and 5 stations – minimize makespan
# Solved with PuLP and the HiGHS solver

import pulp
import itertools

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Jobs: each entry is a list of (Station, Duration) in the required order
jobs = {
    "P1": [("B", 1), ("E", 2), ("D", 7), ("A", 5), ("C", 2)],
    "P2": [("E", 4), ("C", 2), ("A", 9), ("B", 5), ("D", 6)],
    "P3": [("B",10), ("C", 3), ("D", 3), ("E", 1), ("A", 9)],
    "P4": [("E", 7), ("C", 3), ("B", 3), ("A", 9), ("D", 2)],
    "P5": [("B", 3), ("E", 4), ("D", 7), ("A", 6), ("C",10)]
}

# Set of all machines
machines = {"A", "B", "C", "D", "E"}

# Helper: create a unique identifier for each operation
# op_id = (job_name, op_index) where op_index starts at 0
operations = []
proc_time = {}      # processing time of each operation
machine_of = {}     # machine used by each operation
for job, ops in jobs.items():
    for idx, (m, t) in enumerate(ops):
        op = (job, idx)
        operations.append(op)
        proc_time[op] = t
        machine_of[op] = m

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("JobShop_Makespan", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables
# Start time of each operation (continuous, >=0)
S = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "Start",
    operations,
    lowBound=0,
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous
)

# Makespan (continuous, >=0)
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective: minimise makespan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimise_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Job‑precedence constraints (operations of the same product must follow the given order)
for job, ops in jobs.items():
    for k in range(len(ops) - 1):
        op_curr = (job, k)
        op_next = (job, k + 1)
        model += (
            S[op_curr] + proc_time[op_curr] <= S[op_next],
            f"Precedence_{job}_{k}_to_{k+1}"
        )

# 2) Machine capacity (disjunctive) constraints
#    For each pair of operations that need the same machine we introduce a binary variable
#    y_ij = 1  => operation i finishes before j starts
#    y_ij = 0  => operation j finishes before i starts
#    A big‑M value larger than any possible schedule length
M = 200  # safe upper bound (total processing time is 123)

# binary ordering variables stored in a dict keyed by a frozen set of the two ops
y = {}
for m in machines:
    ops_on_m = [op for op in operations if machine_of[op] == m]
    for op_i, op_j in itertools.combinations(ops_on_m, 2):
        var_name = f"Y_{op_i[0]}_{op_i[1]}_before_{op_j[0]}_{op_j[1]}"
        y[(op_i, op_j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat=pulp.LpBinary)

        # i before j
        model += (
            S[op_i] + proc_time[op_i] <= S[op_j] + M * (1 - y[(op_i, op_j)]),
            f"Machine_{m}_order_{op_i}_before_{op_j}"
        )
        # j before i
        model += (
            S[op_j] + proc_time[op_j] <= S[op_i] + M * y[(op_i, op_j)],
            f"Machine_{m}_order_{op_j}_before_{op_i}"
        )

# 3) Makespan definition: Cmax >= completion time of every operation
for op in operations:
    model += Cmax >= S[op] + proc_time[op], f"Makespan_def_{op[0]}_{op[1]}"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print("Status :", pulp.LpStatus[model.status])
print("Minimum makespan (total completion time) =", pulp.value(Cmax))
print("\nStart times (job, operation index) -> start")
for op in sorted(operations):
    print(f"{op} -> {pulp.value(S[op]):.2f}")

# Optional: a readable schedule per machine
print("\nSchedule per station:")
for m in sorted(machines):
    ops_on_m = [op for op in operations if machine_of[op] == m]
    # sort by start time
    ops_on_m.sort(key=lambda o: pulp.value(S[o]))
    print(f"Station {m}:")
    for op in ops_on_m:
        st = pulp.value(S[op])
        ft = st + proc_time[op]
        print(f"  {op[0]} op{op[1]+1} [{st:.2f}, {ft:.2f}] (dur {proc_time[op]})")

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Job‑shop scheduling model for 5 products (jobs) and 5 stations (machines).
Each product follows a fixed sequence of (machine, processing time) pairs.
The model minimizes the makespan (total completion time).

The formulation uses:
 - continuous start‑time variables   s[j, o]
 - continuous makespan variable       Cmax
 - binary ordering variables          y[i,j,m]  (1 if operation i precedes j on machine m)

All constraints are written with <=, >= or == only.
Solved with PuLP + HiGHS.
"""

import pulp

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Data
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
jobs = {
    "P1": [("B", 1), ("E", 2), ("D", 7), ("A", 5), ("C", 2)],
    "P2": [("E", 4), ("C", 2), ("A", 9), ("B", 5), ("D", 6)],
    "P3": [("B",10), ("C", 3), ("D", 3), ("E", 1), ("A", 9)],
    "P4": [("E", 7), ("C", 3), ("B", 3), ("A", 9), ("D", 2)],
    "P5": [("B", 3), ("E", 4), ("D", 7), ("A", 6), ("C",10)]
}

machines = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]

# Create a flat list of operations with identifiers
# op_id = (job, idx) where idx = 0..4 (position in the job's route)
operations = {}
for job, seq in jobs.items():
    for idx, (mach, dur) in enumerate(seq):
        operations[(job, idx)] = {"machine": mach, "duration": dur}

# Big‑M value (larger than any feasible makespan)
M = sum(op["duration"] for op in operations.values()) + 10   # 123 + 10 = 133

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Model
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("JobShop_Makespan_Minimization", pulp.LpMinimize)

# 2.1 Decision variables
# start time of each operation (continuous, >=0)
s = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "Start",
    ((job, idx) for (job, idx) in operations),
    lowBound=0,
    cat=pulp.LpContinuous,
)

# makespan (continuous, >=0)
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Makespan", lowBound=0, cat=pulp.LpContinuous)

# binary ordering variables for every unordered pair of operations that share a machine
y = {}
for mach in machines:
    # collect all operations processed on this machine
    ops_on_m = [op_id for op_id, data in operations.items() if data["machine"] == mach]
    # create binary variables for each unordered pair
    for i in range(len(ops_on_m)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(ops_on_m)):
            op_i = ops_on_m[i]
            op_j = ops_on_m[j]
            var_name = f"Y_{op_i[0]}_{op_i[1]}_before_{op_j[0]}_{op_j[1]}_on_{mach}"
            y[(op_i, op_j, mach)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat=pulp.LpBinary)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Objective
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimize_makespan"

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Constraints
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 4.1 Job‑precedence constraints (operations inside each job must follow the given order)
for job, seq in jobs.items():
    for idx in range(len(seq) - 1):
        cur = (job, idx)
        nxt = (job, idx + 1)
        model += (
            s[nxt] >= s[cur] + operations[cur]["duration"]
        ), f"Precedence_{job}_{idx}_to_{idx+1}"

# 4.2 Machine capacity constraints using the binary ordering variables
for mach in machines:
    ops_on_m = [op_id for op_id, data in operations.items() if data["machine"] == mach]
    for i in range(len(ops_on_m)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(ops_on_m)):
            op_i = ops_on_m[i]
            op_j = ops_on_m[j]
            dur_i = operations[op_i]["duration"]
            dur_j = operations[op_j]["duration"]
            y_ij = y[(op_i, op_j, mach)]

            # If y_ij = 1 then i precedes j
            model += (
                s[op_i] + dur_i <= s[op_j] + M * (1 - y_ij)
            ), f"Machine_{mach}_order_{op_i}_before_{op_j}"
            # If y_ij = 0 then j precedes i
            model += (
                s[op_j] + dur_j <= s[op_i] + M * y_ij
            ), f"Machine_{mach}_order_{op_j}_before_{op_i}"

# 4.3 Makespan definition: every operation must finish no later than Cmax
for op_id, data in operations.items():
    model += (
        s[op_id] + data["duration"] <= Cmax
    ), f"Makespan_bound_{op_id[0]}_{op_id[1]}"

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Solve
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
solver = pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120)
model.solve(solver)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Output
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Optimal makespan: {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times (job, operation index):")
for op_id in sorted(operations):
    print(f"  {op_id}: start = {pulp.value(s[op_id]):.2f}, "
          f"machine = {operations[op_id]['machine']}, "
          f"duration = {operations[op_id]['duration']}")

# Optional: produce a readable schedule per machine
print("\nSchedule per machine:")
for mach in machines:
    print(f" Machine {mach}:")
    # collect ops on this machine, sort by start time
    ops = [op_id for op_id, data in operations.items() if data["machine"] == mach]
    ops_sorted = sorted(ops, key=lambda o: pulp.value(s[o]))
    for op in ops_sorted:
        st = pulp.value(s[op])
        dur = operations[op]["duration"]
        print(f"   {op[0]} (op {op[1]})  [{st:.2f}, {st+dur:.2f}]")

# Jobs are numbered 1..5, operations within a job are indexed 0..4
# Each operation is a tuple (machine, processing_time)

job_ops = {
    1: [("B", 1), ("E", 2), ("D", 7), ("A", 5), ("C", 2)],
    2: [("E", 4), ("C", 2), ("A", 9), ("B", 5), ("D", 6)],

    4: [("E", 7), ("C", 3), ("B", 3), ("A", 9), ("D", 2)],
    5: [("B", 3), ("E", 4), ("D", 7), ("A", 6), ("C",10)],
}

# big‑M (larger than any possible makespan)
M = 200

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("JobShop", pulp.LpMinimize)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Decision variables
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Start time of each operation (continuous, >=0)
start = pulp.LpVariable.dicts(
    "S",
    ((j, o) for j in job_ops for o in range(len(job_ops[j]))),
    lowBound=0,
    cat="Continuous",
)

# Makespan (continuous)
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Cmax", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Binary ordering variables for every unordered pair of operations that share a machine
y = {}   # y[(i1,i2)] = 1  => operation i1 precedes i2
# collect operations per machine
ops_by_machine = {}
for (j, o), (m, p) in (( (j,o), job_ops[j][o]) for j in job_ops for o in range(len(job_ops[j]))):
    ops_by_machine.setdefault(m, []).append((j, o))

for m, ops in ops_by_machine.items():
    for idx1 in range(len(ops)):
        for idx2 in range(idx1+1, len(ops)):
            i1 = ops[idx1]
            i2 = ops[idx2]
            var_name = f"Y_{i1[0]}_{i1[1]}_{i2[0]}_{i2[1]}"
            y[(i1, i2)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimize_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Precedence constraints inside each job (fixed order)
for j, ops in job_ops.items():
    for o in range(len(ops)-1):
        dur = ops[o][1]
        model += (
            start[(j, o+1)] >= start[(j, o)] + dur,
            f"Job_{j}_op_{o}_to_{o+1}",
        )

# 2) Disjunctive (machine capacity) constraints
for m, ops in ops_by_machine.items():
    for idx1 in range(len(ops)):
        for idx2 in range(idx1+1, len(ops)):
            i1 = ops[idx1]   # (j1, o1)
            i2 = ops[idx2]   # (j2, o2)
            dur1 = job_ops[i1[0]][i1[1]][1]

            # if y[(i1,i2)] == 1 then i1 before i2
            model += (
                start[i2] >= start[i1] + dur1 - M * (1 - y[(i1, i2)]),
                f"Seq_{i1}_before_{i2}",
            )
            # if y[(i1,i2)] == 0 then i2 before i1
            model += (
                start[i1] >= start[i2] + dur2 - M * y[(i1, i2)],
                f"Seq_{i2}_before_{i1}",
            )

# 3) Makespan must dominate completion of each job
for j, ops in job_ops.items():
    last_op = len(ops) - 1
    last_dur = ops[last_op][1]
    model += (
        Cmax >= start[(j, last_op)] + last_dur,
        f"Makespan_job_{j}",
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Optimal makespan (Cmax): {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Job‑shop model for the four delivery routes.
Each route = a job, each hub = a machine.
Goal: minimise the makespan (total completion time).

PuLP + HiGHS solver.
"""

import pulp

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Jobs (routes) – list of (hub, processing time) in the required order
jobs = {
    1: [("C", 5), ("B", 5), ("A", 7), ("D", 7)],
    2: [("D", 4), ("A", 5), ("C", 6), ("B", 1)],
    3: [("A", 8), ("B",10), ("C", 2), ("D", 3)],
    4: [("C", 7), ("B", 8), ("A", 1), ("D", 2)],
}

# List of all hubs (machines)
machines = ["A", "B", "C", "D"]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: create a unique key for every operation (job, operation_index)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
ops = []                     # list of all operation keys
proc_time = {}               # processing time for each operation
op_machine = {}              # hub (machine) for each operation

for j, seq in jobs.items():
    for k, (hub, dur) in enumerate(seq):
        key = (j, k)                     # (job_id, position_in_job)
        ops.append(key)
        proc_time[key] = dur
        op_machine[key] = hub

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model = pulp.LpProblem("Delivery_Routes_JobShop", pulp.LpMinimize)

# Decision variables ----------------------------------------------------
# Start time of each operation (continuous, >=0)
S = pulp.LpVariable.dicts("Start", ops, lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Makespan
Cmax = pulp.LpVariable("Makespan", lowBound=0, cat="Continuous")

# Binary ordering variables for every unordered pair of operations that share a hub
# y[(i,j)] = 1  => operation i finishes before j starts
# Only create for pairs on the same machine and belonging to different jobs
y = {}
M = sum(proc_time.values())                     # big‑M (upper bound on any start)

for hub in machines:
    # operations processed on this hub
    hub_ops = [op for op in ops if op_machine[op] == hub]
    # unordered pairs
    for idx1 in range(len(hub_ops)):
        for idx2 in range(idx1 + 1, len(hub_ops)):
            i = hub_ops[idx1]
            j = hub_ops[idx2]
            # If the two operations belong to the same job, their order is already fixed
            if i[0] == j[0]:
                continue
            var_name = f"y_{i[0]}_{i[1]}_before_{j[0]}_{j[1]}"
            y[(i, j)] = pulp.LpVariable(var_name, cat="Binary")
            # also need the reverse variable implicitly (y_ji = 1 - y_ij)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Objective
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model += Cmax, "Minimise_makespan"

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1) Job‑precedence constraints (the given order inside each route)
for j, seq in jobs.items():
    for k in range(len(seq) - 1):
        i = (j, k)
        nxt = (j, k + 1)
        model += (
            S[nxt] >= S[i] + proc_time[i],
            f"Job_{j}_op_{k}_to_{k+1}",
        )

# 2) Disjunctive (machine) constraints using binary ordering variables
for (i, j), y_ij in y.items():
    # i before j
    model += (
        S[j] >= S[i] + proc_time[i] - M * (1 - y_ij),
        f"Machine_{op_machine[i]}_order_{i}_before_{j}",
    )
    # j before i  (using y_ij, because y_ji = 1 - y_ij)
    model += (
        S[i] >= S[j] + proc_time[j] - M * y_ij,
        f"Machine_{op_machine[i]}_order_{j}_before_{i}",
    )

# 3) Makespan must be at least the finishing time of every operation
for op in ops:
    model += (
        Cmax >= S[op] + proc_time[op],
        f"Makespan_covers_job{op[0]}_op{op[1]}",
    )

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Solve
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
model.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False, timeLimit=120))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
print(f"Status: {pulp.LpStatus[model.status]}")
print(f"Optimal makespan: {pulp.value(Cmax)}\n")

print("Start times (job, operation_index) -> start")
for op in sorted(ops):
    print(f"  Job {op[0]}, Op {op[1]} (Hub {op_machine[op]}, dur {proc_time[op]}): "
          f"{pulp.value(S[op]):.2f}")

# Optional: show the order on each hub
print("\nSequence on each hub:")
for hub in machines:
    hub_ops = [op for op in ops if op_machine[op] == hub]
    # sort by start time
    hub_ops_sorted = sorted(hub_ops, key=lambda o: pulp.value(S[o]))
    seq_str = " -> ".join(
        f"J{op[0]}O{op[1]}(start={pulp.value(S[op]):.1f})" for op in hub_ops_sorted
    )
    print(f"  Hub {hub}: {seq_str}")
